data.diagnosis: Cellular angiofibroma of the female genital tract
data.description: A rare benign, usually well-circumscribed mesenchymal tumor that occurs most often in the vulvovaginal region but can arise in the cervix or pelvis. It contains bland spindle cells, collagen, and characteristic prominent hyalinized blood vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Small approximately 3 cm well-defined pelvic or genital-tract mass
Solid lesion identified on MRI, ultrasound, and CT
Grossly circumscribed pale tan-pink soft-tissue tumor
Histology showing bland spindle-cell proliferation with abundant collagen
Numerous prominent small-to-medium-sized vessels in the lesion
No described evidence of aggressive invasion or metastasis

data.description: A benign mesenchymal tumor of the lower female genital tract, usually occurring as a small, slow-growing, sharply circumscribed vulvovaginal or cervical mass. Microscopically it contains stromal spindle or epithelioid cells clustered around numerous thin-walled blood vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Small, circumscribed genital-tract or pelvic mass
Benign-appearing imaging characteristics
Grossly well-demarcated soft-tissue lesion
Spindle-cell stromal histology
Prominent vascular component
Lack of reported metastatic disease
symptoms_not_in_common: The conspicuous collagen-rich or fibrous appearance may be more characteristic of cellular angiofibroma than classic angiomyofibroblastoma
No vulvar or vaginal symptoms are described

data.description: A rare locally infiltrative benign-to-low-grade mesenchymal tumor affecting the pelvis, perineum, vulva, or vagina, typically in women of reproductive age. It is often myxoid and vascular and may show a swirling internal pattern on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic or genital-tract soft-tissue mass
Vascular stromal lesion on pathology
Spindle-cell mesenchymal tumor
Possible internal swirling appearance on MRI
May occur in the female pelvis
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion is relatively small at approximately 3 cm; aggressive angiomyxomas are often much larger at presentation
The mass appears well circumscribed rather than deeply infiltrative
Histology appears collagenous/fibrous rather than predominantly hypocellular myxoid stroma
No reported pelvic pressure, pain, vulvar enlargement, or recurrent infiltrative disease

data.description: Ischemic necrosis of splenic tissue, usually caused by arterial embolism, thrombosis, hypercoagulability, hematologic disease, trauma, or vasculitis. Imaging commonly shows peripheral wedge-shaped hypoechoic and nonenhancing splenic areas with reduced vascular flow.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple peripheral wedge-shaped focal splenic abnormalities on ultrasound and MRI
Areas with little or no Doppler vascularity
Appearance compatible with nonenhancing ischemic splenic parenchyma

data.description: Localized infectious collections in the spleen caused by bacterial, fungal, mycobacterial, or parasitic infection. They may appear as multiple hypoechoic lesions on ultrasound and focal lesions on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple focal splenic lesions
Hypoechoic abnormalities on ultrasound
Focal lesions that may show altered or reduced internal vascularity
symptoms_not_in_common: Wedge-shaped peripheral morphology is more characteristic of infarction than abscess

data.description: Lymphoma can involve the spleen as diffuse enlargement, multiple hypoechoic nodules, or focal masses. It may occur as part of systemic Hodgkin or non-Hodgkin lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple focal splenic lesions
Hypoechoic splenic lesions on ultrasound
Abnormal focal splenic signal on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Peripheral wedge-shaped lesions with absent perfusion are less typical of lymphoma
No lymphadenopathy, constitutional symptoms, or known malignancy is provided

data.description: Sarcoidosis is a systemic granulomatous inflammatory disease that can involve the spleen, producing multiple small hypoechoic nodules that are often relatively hypointense on MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple focal splenic nodules
Hypoechoic splenic abnormalities on ultrasound
Multifocal splenic signal abnormalities on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Wedge-shaped peripheral distribution and markedly reduced vascularity favor infarction rather than granulomatous nodules
No pulmonary, lymph-node, skin, or systemic sarcoidosis findings are reported

data.description: Hydatid disease is infection by Echinococcus species, endemic in parts of Spain. Splenic involvement is uncommon and typically produces cystic lesions, sometimes with daughter cysts, membranes, or calcified walls.
symptoms_in_common: Residence in Spain, where Echinococcus exposure can occur
Focal splenic lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: The depicted lesions appear solid or wedge-shaped rather than typical cystic hydatid lesions
No daughter cysts, detached membranes, or calcified cyst wall are evident from the provided images

data.description: A parasitic liver infection caused by the liver fluke Fasciola hepatica, which is endemic in parts of Spain. During the hepatic migratory phase it can produce clustered, irregular hypodense liver lesions or inflammatory masses on CT.
symptoms_in_common: Residence in Spain, where Fasciola hepatica can occur
Heterogeneous focal hepatic lesion on CT
Possible smaller adjacent hepatic lesions compatible with parasitic migration tracks or inflammatory foci
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever reported
No right-upper-quadrant abdominal pain reported
No eosinophilia reported
No jaundice or biliary symptoms reported

data.description: A zoonotic infection caused by Echinococcus granulosus that commonly affects the liver and is endemic in Mediterranean areas, including Spain. It may appear as a hepatic cystic mass with internal daughter cysts, membranes, calcification, or complicated inflammatory changes.
symptoms_in_common: Residence in Spain, an area where cystic echinococcosis occurs
Large focal lesion in the liver on CT
Possible internal heterogeneous or cystic-appearing components within the lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: Classic well-defined cyst with daughter cysts is not clearly demonstrated
No exposure to dogs, sheep, or livestock reported
No abdominal pain reported
No eosinophilia reported
No jaundice reported

data.description: A primary malignant tumor of the liver, usually arising in the setting of cirrhosis, chronic hepatitis B or C infection, alcohol-associated liver disease, or other chronic liver disorders. It can present as a large heterogeneous liver mass with necrosis and satellite nodules.
symptoms_in_common: Large heterogeneous hepatic mass on CT
Possible additional small hepatic lesion that could represent a satellite nodule
symptoms_not_in_common: No cirrhosis reported
No chronic viral hepatitis reported
No chronic liver disease symptoms reported
No weight loss reported
No abdominal pain reported
No jaundice reported

data.description: A mitochondrial inherited optic neuropathy causing subacute, usually painless central visual loss and progressive optic-nerve atrophy, often affecting both eyes.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral optic-disc pallor/optic atrophy on fundus photographs
Marked bilateral retinal nerve fiber layer thinning on OCT
Relatively symmetric involvement of both optic nerves
symptoms_not_in_common: Brain or spinal cord MRI abnormalities are not a typical primary feature of isolated LHON
No history of subacute central visual loss, dyschromatopsia, or maternal family history is provided

data.description: An immune-mediated demyelinating disease of the central nervous system that can cause optic neuritis, optic-nerve atrophy, and lesions in the brain and spinal cord.
symptoms_in_common: Optic-nerve atrophy with reduced retinal nerve fiber layer thickness
Possible central nervous system involvement suggested by brain and spinal MRI images
Bilateral optic nerve damage can occur after recurrent or bilateral optic neuritis
symptoms_not_in_common: No episodes of painful visual loss are reported
No sensory, motor, balance, bladder, or other neurologic relapses are described
The displayed brain MRI does not clearly show the characteristic multifocal periventricular demyelinating lesions

data.description: An autoimmune astrocytopathy, commonly associated with aquaporin-4 antibodies, characterized by severe optic neuritis and myelitis that may produce persistent optic atrophy.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral optic nerve damage and retinal nerve fiber layer loss
Spinal MRI evaluation is relevant because myelitis is a key manifestation
Brain MRI may be normal or nonspecific in some patients
symptoms_not_in_common: No severe acute optic neuritis episode is described
No longitudinally extensive spinal cord lesion is clearly visible in the provided image
No myelitis symptoms such as limb weakness, numbness, urinary retention, or bowel dysfunction are reported

data.description: An inflammatory demyelinating disorder that can cause unilateral or bilateral optic neuritis, myelitis, and brain lesions; residual optic atrophy may occur after optic neuritis.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral optic neuropathy/optic atrophy
Thinning of the retinal nerve fiber layer in both eyes
Brain and spinal cord imaging is appropriate when evaluating inflammatory optic neuritis
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute optic neuritis symptoms, including eye pain or sudden visual loss, are provided
No myelitis, encephalitis, or acute demyelinating neurologic syndrome is described
No optic nerve enhancement or characteristic inflammatory MRI lesions are shown

data.diagnosis: Harding syndrome (LHON with multiple sclerosis-like demyelinating disease)
data.description: A rare overlap syndrome in which a patient with a mitochondrial LHON mutation develops optic neuropathy together with multiple-sclerosis-like central nervous system demyelination.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral optic atrophy and severe retinal nerve fiber layer thinning compatible with LHON-type optic neuropathy
Presence of both optic nerve findings and brain/spinal MRI assessment raises the possibility of a demyelinating overlap disorder
This condition is reported in European populations, including Spain
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical history of relapsing neurologic symptoms is provided
No clearly characteristic demyelinating lesions are visible on the supplied brain MRI image
No mitochondrial genetic testing result or maternal family history is given

An autosomal-recessive disorder caused by pathogenic ATP7B variants, resulting in impaired biliary copper excretion and toxic copper accumulation, especially in the liver, brain, and cornea.
symptoms_in_common: Pathogenic ATP7B c.2333G>T (p.Arg778Leu) variant reported in a homozygous/pure combination state
Bilateral basal ganglia abnormalities on brain MRI, compatible with copper-related neurologic involvement
T1 basal-ganglia hyperintensity suggesting abnormal metal deposition
T2, diffusion, and FLAIR basal-ganglia signal abnormalities

data.diagnosis: Neurodegeneration with brain iron accumulation (NBIA), including pantothenate kinase-associated neurodegeneration
data.description: A group of inherited neurodegenerative disorders characterized by abnormal iron deposition in the basal ganglia, usually causing dystonia, parkinsonism, cognitive decline, or other movement disorders.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral basal ganglia involvement on MRI
MRI appearance suggesting abnormal metal deposition in deep brain nuclei
symptoms_not_in_common: Pathogenic ATP7B variant, which specifically supports Wilson disease rather than NBIA
Corneal ring appearance consistent with Kayser-Fleischer rings
Liver biopsy abnormalities suggesting hepatic involvement
Basal ganglia T1 hyperintensity, whereas iron deposition more commonly produces T2 or susceptibility-related hypointensity

data.diagnosis: Acquired hepatocerebral degeneration due to chronic liver disease or portosystemic shunting
data.description: A neurologic complication of advanced chronic liver disease in which manganese and other metabolic toxins accumulate in the brain, often producing bilateral globus pallidus or basal ganglia T1 hyperintensity.
symptoms_in_common: T1 hyperintensity in the basal ganglia compatible with metal deposition
Evidence of liver pathology on biopsy
Bilateral deep gray matter MRI abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Pathogenic homozygous/pure-combination ATP7B c.2333G>T variant
Corneal Kayser-Fleischer ring appearance
T2, diffusion, and FLAIR basal-ganglia abnormalities more suggestive of direct Wilson-related basal ganglia injury than isolated manganese deposition

data.description: A bacterial infection of the deeper skin and subcutaneous tissues, usually causing a warm, tender, expanding red area.
symptoms_in_common: Localized red to violaceous skin discoloration around the elbow
Possible swelling of the involved area
Ill-defined erythematous patches
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple separated or annular-looking lesions rather than one uniformly expanding area
No visible skin break, drainage, or pus
No fever or systemic symptoms reported

data.diagnosis: Arthropod bite reaction (including mosquito, flea, bedbug, or other insect bite hypersensitivity)
data.description: A localized inflammatory or allergic skin reaction following an arthropod bite, often producing itchy red papules, plaques, or swollen areas.
symptoms_in_common: Several red papules or plaques on the arm near the elbow
Localized swelling and inflammation
Grouped distribution of skin lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: No bite punctum is clearly visible
No itch, exposure history, or recent outdoor/insect contact reported
The larger violaceous lesion may be more extensive than typical uncomplicated bites

data.diagnosis: Erythema migrans due to Lyme borreliosis
data.description: An expanding skin lesion caused by Borrelia infection after a tick bite; it may appear as a red expanding patch and is not always a classic bull's-eye rash.
symptoms_in_common: Red expanding-appearing patches or plaques
Possible annular or target-like appearance of some lesions
Outdoor tick exposure is possible in Spain
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple clustered lesions near one elbow are less typical than a single expanding lesion
No reported tick bite
No reported fever, fatigue, headache, muscle aches, or joint pains
No clearly defined expanding ring with central clearing

data.description: An inflammatory skin disorder characterized by tender red-to-violaceous papules, nodules, or plaques, frequently on the upper limbs, sometimes with fever or elevated inflammatory markers.
symptoms_in_common: Red to violaceous raised-appearing plaques or nodules
Upper-extremity involvement
Lesions with a pseudovesicular or edematous appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or systemic illness reported
No reported painful tenderness
No history provided of inflammatory disease, medication exposure, blood disorder, or malignancy

data.description: An inflammatory reaction of subcutaneous fat causing tender red or bruise-like nodules, classically on the shins but occasionally at other sites.
symptoms_in_common: Red-to-purple bruise-like inflammatory lesions
Nodular or plaque-like appearance
Possible evolution toward violaceous coloration
symptoms_not_in_common: Location near the elbow is atypical; lesions usually occur on the lower legs
No reported painful nodules
No fever, joint pain, respiratory illness, gastrointestinal symptoms, or medication trigger reported

data.description: A symptomatic elongated styloid process or ossified stylohyoid ligament that can irritate nearby throat, cranial nerve, or vascular structures.
symptoms_in_common: CT appearance of an elongated ossified stylohyoid complex extending from the skull base toward the hyoid region
symptoms_not_in_common: No throat or neck pain was reported
No foreign-body sensation in the throat was reported
No pain with swallowing was reported
No facial pain, ear pain, headache, or dizziness was reported

data.description: Mineralization of the ligament between the styloid process and hyoid bone; it may be an incidental imaging finding or may contribute to Eagle syndrome when symptomatic.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent linear ossified structure along the expected course of the stylohyoid ligament on sagittal CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms were provided
No swallowing difficulty was reported
No neck movement-related pain was reported

data.description: An anatomical variant in which the temporal bone styloid process is longer than usual; it is often asymptomatic but can be associated with Eagle syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging suggests an unusually long mineralized styloid-stylohyoid structure
symptoms_not_in_common: No symptoms suggesting nerve irritation were reported
No throat discomfort was reported
No referred ear pain was reported
No vascular symptoms such as transient neurologic deficits or syncope were reported

A pancreatic neuroendocrine tumor that secretes insulin inappropriately, causing fasting or recurrent hypoglycemia with elevated endogenous insulin and C-peptide levels.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hypoglycemia: glucose 2.4 mmol/L
Inappropriately elevated insulin during hypoglycemia: 574.0 pmol/L
Elevated C-peptide indicating endogenous insulin production: 3.214 nmol/L
Suppressed beta-hydroxybutyrate during hypoglycemia, consistent with insulin-mediated inhibition of ketone production

data.description: Hypoglycemia caused by insulin-secretagogue medications, which stimulate pancreatic insulin secretion and produce high insulin and C-peptide levels similar to insulinoma.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hypoglycemia: glucose 2.4 mmol/L
Elevated insulin during hypoglycemia
Elevated C-peptide due to stimulated endogenous insulin release
Low beta-hydroxybutyrate due to insulin excess
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of diabetes treatment, sulfonylurea use, meglitinide use, or accidental medication exposure is provided

data.description: A condition involving diffuse pancreatic beta-cell hyperfunction, resulting in excessive endogenous insulin release and recurrent hypoglycemia; it may occur after bariatric surgery or without a clear cause.
symptoms_in_common: Hypoglycemia
High endogenous insulin concentration
High C-peptide concentration
Suppressed ketone production during hypoglycemia
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of post-meal hypoglycemia is provided
No history of bariatric surgery or gastrointestinal surgery is provided

data.description: A rare autoimmune disorder in which insulin autoantibodies bind insulin and can cause episodes of hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia without exogenous insulin administration.
symptoms_in_common: Hypoglycemia
Elevated insulin level
Elevated C-peptide level consistent with endogenous insulin secretion
Low beta-hydroxybutyrate consistent with insulin effect
symptoms_not_in_common: Insulin levels in insulin autoimmune syndrome are often extremely high, frequently much higher than the reported value
No insulin antibody results are provided
No associated autoimmune disease or triggering medication exposure is provided

data.description: A painful hypermobility of the false ribs, usually the 8th to 10th ribs, caused by laxity or disruption of interchondral attachments. Dynamic ultrasound may show abnormal movement or overriding of a rib over an adjacent rib.
symptoms_in_common: Ultrasound appearance involving adjacent false ribs (7th, 8th, and 9th ribs)
Apparent prominence or abnormal position of the 8th rib relative to neighboring ribs
symptoms_not_in_common: No rib or upper abdominal pain was provided
No clicking, popping, or movement-related symptoms were provided
No tenderness or symptoms triggered by coughing, twisting, or deep breathing were provided

data.diagnosis: Healed or healing rib fracture with callus formation
data.description: A prior rib fracture may heal with bony callus, cortical irregularity, thickening, or angulation that can create an abnormal contour on ultrasound.
symptoms_in_common: Irregular or prominent contour of the 8th rib on ultrasound
Possible alteration in alignment relative to the adjacent 7th and 9th ribs
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of chest trauma was provided
No localized chest-wall pain was provided
No pain with breathing, coughing, or palpation was provided

data.diagnosis: Congenital rib deformity or rib fusion
data.description: A congenital chest-wall variation can produce an abnormal rib shape, partial fusion, bifid rib, or atypical spacing between adjacent ribs. These findings may be incidental or associated with chest-wall asymmetry.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal apparent anatomy or spacing among the 7th, 8th, and 9th ribs on ultrasound
Possible deformity centered on the 8th rib
symptoms_not_in_common: No lifelong chest-wall asymmetry was reported
No developmental history was provided
No respiratory symptoms or functional limitation was provided

data.description: A benign or secondary condition in which multiple gas-filled cysts develop within the bowel wall, usually in the submucosa or subserosa. It can appear as polypoid lesions at colonoscopy and as clustered radiolucent cysts on contrast imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple cyst-like or polypoid lesions in the colonic wall on imaging
Submucosal-appearing, smooth colonic protrusions at endoscopy
Endoscopic ultrasound appearance compatible with gas-containing intramural cysts
Histology showing empty cystic spaces with inflammatory or giant-cell reaction
symptoms_not_in_common: No patient-reported gastrointestinal symptoms were provided
No abdominal pain, distension, diarrhea, rectal bleeding, fever, or obstructive symptoms were reported

data.description: A rare benign malformation characterized by dilated lymphatic channels in the bowel wall, producing multiple submucosal cystic lesions that may resemble pneumatosis.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple smooth submucosal cystic-appearing colonic lesions
Potentially incidental finding without reported clinical symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: The imaging appearance suggests intramural gas rather than fluid-filled lymphatic spaces
Histologic giant-cell reaction around empty spaces is more characteristic of pneumatosis
No patient-reported gastrointestinal symptoms were provided

data.description: A benign disorder in which mucin-filled cystically dilated colonic glands extend into the submucosa, often associated with chronic inflammation, rectal prolapse, or inflammatory bowel disease.
symptoms_in_common: Cystic or polypoid lesions involving the colonic wall
May produce submucosal-appearing lesions at endoscopy
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesions shown appear gas-filled rather than mucin-filled glandular cysts
No rectal bleeding, mucus discharge, chronic diarrhea, rectal prolapse, or inflammatory bowel disease symptoms were reported
No patient-reported gastrointestinal symptoms were provided

data.description: Marked eosinophilia (53.5%) with mild leukocytosis, anemia (Hgb 8.6 g/dL), elevated CRP (2.66 mg/dL), elevated IgE (254 IU/mL), and mildly elevated TARC (119 pg/mL). ANA, RF, Jo-1 antibody, PR-ANCA, MPO-ANCA, and hepatitis B/C and HIV markers were negative. Arterial blood gas showed alkalemia with low pCO2 and mild hypoxemia.

data.diagnosis: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia, not otherwise specified (CEL-NOS)
data.description: A clonal myeloid neoplasm characterized by persistent eosinophilia, abnormal immature/dysplastic eosinophils, and evidence of a myeloid malignancy when defining PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, or PCM1-JAK2 rearrangements are absent.
symptoms_in_common: Marked eosinophilia (53.5%)
Mild leukocytosis
Anemia (hemoglobin 8.6 g/dL)
Circulating immature eosinophil precursors including eosinophilic bands, metamyelocytes, and myelocytes
Dysplastic hematologic morphology including irregular hypersegmented neutrophils and megaloblasts
Chromosomal abnormalities involving chromosomes 1 and 7
Elevated inflammatory marker (CRP)
Mild hypoxemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Mildly elevated IgE is more often associated with reactive/allergic eosinophilia, although it can occur in CEL
Mildly elevated TARC is not a defining feature of CEL-NOS
Respiratory alkalosis is not a defining hematologic feature

data.diagnosis: Myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia and tyrosine-kinase gene rearrangement
data.description: A group of clonal hematologic neoplasms associated with eosinophilia and rearrangements involving genes such as PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, or PCM1-JAK2. These disorders may resemble chronic eosinophilic leukemia and can show myeloid dysplasia and anemia.
symptoms_in_common: Marked eosinophilia
Leukocytosis
Anemia
Immature eosinophilic granulocyte forms in peripheral blood
Possible clonal cytogenetic abnormality
Elevated CRP
Hypoxemia, potentially from eosinophilic pulmonary involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: The provided chromosome abnormalities involving chromosomes 1 and 7 are not the classic cytogenetic pattern for PDGFRA, PDGFRB, FGFR1, or PCM1-JAK2 rearrangements
Elevated IgE is not a defining feature
Elevated TARC is not a defining feature
Negative ANCA and other autoimmune serologies do not specifically support this diagnosis

data.description: A syndrome of persistent, otherwise unexplained eosinophilia that can cause inflammatory organ injury, particularly involving the lungs, heart, skin, nervous system, and gastrointestinal tract. It is diagnosed after exclusion of secondary causes and clonal eosinophilic neoplasms.
symptoms_in_common: Marked eosinophilia
Mild leukocytosis
Elevated IgE
Elevated CRP
Mild hypoxemia
Respiratory alkalosis, which may occur with pulmonary involvement
Negative autoimmune and viral serologies
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked anemia is less typical in idiopathic HES
Megaloblastic and dysplastic blood-cell morphology is not typical
Eosinophilic myelocytes, metamyelocytes, and bands with apparent dysplasia favor a clonal myeloid process
Cytogenetic abnormalities involving chromosomes 1 and 7 would argue against idiopathic HES

data.description: An eosinophil-rich necrotizing vasculitis that typically occurs in patients with asthma, allergic rhinosinusitis, pulmonary infiltrates, neuropathy, and systemic inflammation. ANCA may be negative in many affected patients.
symptoms_in_common: Marked eosinophilia
Elevated IgE
Elevated CRP
Mild hypoxemia
Negative MPO-ANCA and PR3-ANCA do not exclude EGPA
symptoms_not_in_common: No asthma is reported
No chronic rhinosinusitis or nasal polyps are reported
No neuropathy, skin purpura, renal disease, or other vasculitic manifestations are reported
Anemia with megaloblastic/dysplastic blood morphology is not typical
Immature eosinophilic precursors and chromosomal abnormalities favor a hematologic neoplasm rather than EGPA

data.description: A CD30-positive T-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma, often occurring in children and adolescents, that can involve lymph nodes and extranodal sites such as bowel, skin, bone, lung, and kidneys. The histology and immunostaining pattern shown are highly suggestive of this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal lymphadenopathy
Possible bowel involvement with dilated bowel loops
Multifocal abdominal and retroperitoneal disease
Renal lesions or renal infiltration
Thoracic lymph node or pulmonary involvement
FDG-avid disseminated disease on PET imaging
Large atypical lymphoid cells on histology
Strong CD30-positive tumor-cell staining
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as fever, night sweats, weight loss, skin lesions, or bone pain are provided
Location in Spain is not a disease symptom

data.description: A B-cell lymphoma characterized by Hodgkin/Reed-Sternberg cells, usually CD30-positive, that commonly presents with lymphadenopathy and may spread to mediastinal and abdominal lymph nodes.
symptoms_in_common: Lymphadenopathy in the chest and abdomen
Possible disseminated nodal disease
FDG-avid lymph nodes on PET imaging
CD30-positive cells may be present
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent extranodal renal and bowel involvement is less typical than in anaplastic large cell lymphoma
The histologic appearance of numerous large anaplastic cells is less typical for classical Hodgkin lymphoma
No reported B symptoms such as fever, drenching night sweats, or unintentional weight loss
Location in Spain is not a disease symptom

data.description: A highly aggressive B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that frequently affects children and often presents with rapidly growing abdominal disease, bowel involvement, mesenteric lymphadenopathy, and possible renal infiltration.
symptoms_in_common: Abdominal mass-like or nodal disease
Possible bowel involvement and bowel-loop dilatation
Mesenteric or retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy
Possible renal involvement
Rapidly disseminated FDG-avid disease can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: CD30 expression and the illustrated anaplastic-cell morphology are not typical of Burkitt lymphoma
Burkitt lymphoma more typically shows a starry-sky histologic pattern rather than anaplastic large cells
Thoracic lymph node involvement is less characteristic at presentation
No reported rapidly enlarging abdominal mass, severe abdominal pain, or tumor-lysis syndrome
Location in Spain is not a disease symptom

diagnoses.name: Mixed-cellularity subtype of classic Hodgkin's lymphoma
diagnoses.title: Mixed cellularity classical Hodgkin lymphoma

data.description: Initial evaluation showed thrombocytopenia (platelets 24,000/µL), neutrophilia with marked lymphopenia, elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit, mild hyponatremia, low chloride, creatinine 1.64 mg/dL, low magnesium, elevated AST/ALT, hyperbilirubinemia with elevated direct bilirubin, and very low haptoglobin.

Acute malaria caused by Plasmodium falciparum, which can produce high parasitemia, hemolysis, thrombocytopenia, hepatic dysfunction, and acute kidney injury. The rapid malaria test and blood smear showing multiple delicate ring forms, including peripheral/appliqué forms, strongly support this diagnosis.
symptoms_in_common: Marked thrombocytopenia (platelets 24,000/µL)
Very low haptoglobin consistent with intravascular hemolysis
Hyperbilirubinemia including elevated direct bilirubin
Elevated AST and ALT
Acute kidney injury with creatinine 1.64 mg/dL
Neutrophilia with marked lymphopenia
Mild hyponatremia
Blood smear with intraerythrocytic ring forms compatible with Plasmodium falciparum
Positive rapid diagnostic test pattern compatible with P. falciparum
Possible splenic enlargement on abdominal ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: Elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit, which may reflect dehydration/hemoconcentration rather than the usual malarial anemia
Low chloride
Low magnesium

data.description: Malaria due to P. falciparum without definite evidence of life-threatening organ dysfunction. However, this patient has laboratory findings concerning for severe rather than uncomplicated disease.
symptoms_in_common: Thrombocytopenia
Hemolysis with low haptoglobin
Hyperbilirubinemia
Elevated liver enzymes
Lymphopenia
Peripheral blood smear showing ring-stage malaria parasites
Rapid malaria test compatible with P. falciparum
symptoms_not_in_common: Creatinine elevation suggesting renal involvement
Profound thrombocytopenia of 24,000/µL
Marked hepatic dysfunction
Elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit rather than anemia

data.description: Malaria caused by P. vivax, typically associated with enlarged red cells, trophozoites, Schüffner stippling, thrombocytopenia, and possible splenomegaly. It is less consistent with the rapid-test and smear morphology shown.
symptoms_in_common: Thrombocytopenia
Possible splenic enlargement
Hyperbilirubinemia and hemolysis
Elevated liver enzymes
Mild renal dysfunction can occur in severe cases
Intraerythrocytic parasites on peripheral blood smear
symptoms_not_in_common: Rapid diagnostic test pattern supportive of P. falciparum rather than isolated P. vivax
Numerous delicate ring forms and peripheral/appliqué forms, which favor P. falciparum
No described enlarged erythrocytes or Schüffner stippling
Elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit rather than anemia

data.description: A tick-borne intraerythrocytic protozoal infection that can resemble malaria on blood smear and may cause hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, jaundice, liver enzyme elevation, and renal injury. The malaria rapid test and parasite morphology favor malaria instead.
symptoms_in_common: Thrombocytopenia
Hemolysis with very low haptoglobin
Hyperbilirubinemia
Elevated AST and ALT
Acute kidney injury
Intraerythrocytic organisms on peripheral smear
Possible splenic involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Rapid diagnostic test consistent with Plasmodium falciparum
Blood-smear morphology favoring malaria ring forms rather than Babesia tetrads or Maltese-cross forms
No reported tick exposure
Elevated hemoglobin and hematocrit rather than the more typical hemolytic anemia

data.description: A full-thickness defect in the esophageal wall allowing saliva, food material, contrast, or infected fluid to enter the mediastinum; this is a medical emergency.
symptoms_in_common: Endoscopic appearance of an esophageal defect communicating with the mediastinum
Contrast extravasation into the mediastinum on fluoroscopic imaging
Visible mediastinal pus on endoscopy
Endoscopic placement of a covered esophageal stent consistent with treatment of a perforation

data.description: Severe infection and inflammation of the mediastinal tissues, commonly caused by esophageal perforation and leakage of contaminated esophageal contents.
symptoms_in_common: Purulent material labeled as mediastinal pus
Communication between the esophagus and mediastinum
Need for endoscopic drainage and/or esophageal stenting
Radiographic evidence of leakage into the mediastinum

data.description: An abnormal tract or persistent opening between the esophagus and mediastinum, often developing after esophageal injury, surgery, infection, or perforation.

data.description: 24 days before admission to MGH, labs showed marked leukocytosis with neutrophilia (WBC 24,000/mm³, 93.8% neutrophils), hyponatremia (124 mmol/L), hyperkalemia (6.0 mmol/L), elevated BUN (30 mg/dL), hypoalbuminemia (2.5 g/dL), and markedly elevated AST (440 U/L). data.description: Initial laboratory findings showed hypophosphatemia with elevated alkaline phosphatase and FGF23, with calcium, creatinine, PTH, and vitamin D values recorded over follow-up. At 3-year follow-up, phosphate remained low at 0.53 mmol/L and C-FGF23 increased to 2050 U/L; at 4 years, phosphate was 0.65 mmol/L and C-FGF23 decreased to 54 U/L. data.description: Progressive acute illness over several days with marked laboratory deterioration: worsening anemia (hemoglobin 14.0 to 9.9 g/dl; hematocrit 41.0% to 26.8%), thrombocytopenia (78,000 to 14,000/mm3) with large platelets, and leukocytosis after initial leukopenia (2,600 to 13,600/mm3) with left shift/bandemia. data.description: An uncommon malignant pancreatic epithelial tumor showing acinar differentiation. It can form a large, circumscribed solid mass with necrosis and hemorrhage.

Solid yellow-tan tumor with hemorrhagic and necrotic areas
Tumor cells arranged in sheets or compact cellular areas

data.description: A rare malignant pancreatic tumor, predominantly occurring in children, with acinar differentiation and characteristic squamoid corpuscles. Adult cases are uncommon.

Possible solid, heterogeneous mass with hemorrhage or necrosis
Cellular tumor with solid growth areas
symptoms_not_in_common: No age is provided; pancreatoblastoma is most typical in young children

data.description: A genetic disorder of keratinization characterized by greasy, crusted, hyperkeratotic papules and plaques, often in seborrheic or flexural areas. Histology typically shows acantholytic dyskeratosis with corps ronds and grains.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple hyperkeratotic, verrucous papules coalescing into plaques
Predominant involvement of the axillary/flexural region
Brown hyperpigmentation and crusting
Comedo-like keratotic plugs
Histology compatible with acantholysis and dyskeratosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No nail abnormalities are described
No mucosal lesions are described
No generalized seborrheic-area eruption is described

data.description: An inherited acantholytic skin disorder causing recurrent painful erosions, fissures, crusted plaques, and maceration in intertriginous sites such as the axillae, groin, and neck.
symptoms_in_common: Axillary/intertriginous involvement
Eroded and crusted areas within plaques
Histologic acantholysis can be present
Chronic plaque-like skin changes in a flexural area
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked verrucous hyperkeratosis is less typical
Numerous comedo-like keratin plugs are not typical
Hyperpigmented papillomatous plaques are more suggestive of Darier disease or an epidermal nevus

data.description: A benign cutaneous mosaic disorder producing persistent linear or localized hyperpigmented, rough, papillomatous, or verrucous plaques, usually beginning early in life.
symptoms_in_common: Localized unilateral-appearing hyperpigmented plaque
Verrucous and papillomatous surface texture
Persistent grouped keratotic papules
Possible involvement along a developmental or mosaic distribution
symptoms_not_in_common: Acantholytic dyskeratosis on histology is not typical of a conventional epidermal nevus
Crusting and erosions are not typical unless secondarily irritated
The flexural distribution and greasy keratotic papules favor Darier disease

data.description: A follicular hamartoma characterized by grouped dilated follicular openings filled with dark keratin plugs, resembling comedones; lesions may become inflamed or form verrucous plaques.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple dark comedo-like keratin plugs
Localized clustered distribution
Hyperpigmented plaque with follicular-appearing openings
Occasional inflamed or crusted lesions may occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse verrucous plaque formation is less typical
Acantholysis and dyskeratosis on histology would not be expected
The prominent flexural papules and crusting are more consistent with Darier disease

data.description: A malignant cartilage-producing bone tumor that commonly arises in the pelvis and may form a large expansile lytic bone lesion with characteristic chondroid matrix calcifications.
symptoms_in_common: Large destructive expansile lesion centered in the left iliac bone
Lobulated soft-tissue mass extending beyond the bone
Internal calcified chondroid matrix with ring-and-arc or stippled appearance on CT/radiography
High signal, lobulated appearance on MRI compatible with a cartilage-rich tumor
Increased metabolic activity on PET imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, age, duration of symptoms, or laboratory findings were provided

data.description: A rare, aggressive subtype of chondrosarcoma composed of undifferentiated small cells and cartilage, often affecting the pelvis and producing a destructive mass with areas of calcification.
symptoms_in_common: Aggressive-appearing iliac bone destruction
Large associated extraosseous soft-tissue mass
Foci of mineralization/calcification within the mass
PET-avid lesion suggesting metabolically active neoplasm
symptoms_not_in_common: The imaging appears markedly lobulated and cartilage-rich, which may be more typical of conventional chondrosarcoma
No patient age or histologic findings were provided

data.description: A malignant primary bone tumor that produces osteoid matrix and can occur in the pelvis, causing destructive bone change, a large soft-tissue mass, and internal mineralization.
symptoms_in_common: Destructive lesion involving the iliac bone
Large soft-tissue component
Internal mineralization/calcification
Hypermetabolic uptake on PET imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: The calcification pattern appears more compatible with chondroid matrix than cloud-like osteoid matrix
No aggressive periosteal reaction or classic osteosarcoma bone formation pattern is clearly shown
No clinical symptoms, age, or laboratory findings were provided

A rare autoimmune neurologic disorder characterized by progressive axial and limb stiffness, painful muscle spasms, and motor hyperexcitability; high-titer glutamic acid decarboxylase (GAD) antibodies are common.
symptoms_in_common: Classical stiff-person syndrome phenotype
Continuous motor unit activity on EMG
Blink-reflex hyperexcitability
Very high anti-GAD antibody level (>2000 U/mL)
Severe mobility impairment requiring a wheelchair before HSCT
Clinical improvement after immunotherapy/HSCT
symptoms_not_in_common: No symptoms or findings in the case are substantially atypical for classic anti-GAD stiff-person syndrome

data.diagnosis: Progressive encephalomyelitis with rigidity and myoclonus (PERM)
data.description: A severe stiff-person-spectrum disorder with rigidity, stimulus-sensitive spasms, myoclonus, brainstem dysfunction, autonomic symptoms, and sometimes encephalopathy; it is often associated with glycine-receptor antibodies but may overlap with anti-GAD autoimmunity.
symptoms_in_common: Motor hyperexcitability with continuous motor unit activity
Blink-reflex hyperexcitability
Severe disabling rigidity/mobility impairment
Response to immunomodulatory treatment
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported myoclonus
No encephalopathy or altered mental status
No brainstem symptoms such as dysphagia, dysarthria, or eye-movement abnormalities
No autonomic instability
High anti-GAD antibodies favor classic stiff-person syndrome rather than typical glycine-receptor-associated PERM

data.description: An autoimmune cerebellar syndrome associated with high-titer GAD antibodies, typically causing gait and limb ataxia, dysarthria, nystagmus, and impaired coordination; it can coexist with other anti-GAD neurologic syndromes.
symptoms_in_common: High-titer anti-GAD antibodies
Impaired walking before treatment
Potential response to immunotherapy
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported gait or limb ataxia
No dysarthria
No nystagmus or other ocular cerebellar signs
Continuous motor unit activity and blink-reflex hyperexcitability are more characteristic of stiff-person syndrome

data.description: A peripheral nerve hyperexcitability disorder causing muscle twitching, cramps, stiffness, myokymia, delayed muscle relaxation, and characteristic spontaneous repetitive discharges on EMG; it is often associated with CASPR2 or LGI1 antibodies.
symptoms_in_common: Muscle hyperexcitability
Stiffness with marked functional disability
Abnormal continuous EMG activity
symptoms_not_in_common: Very high anti-GAD antibodies are more supportive of stiff-person syndrome
Blink-reflex hyperexcitability is more consistent with central nervous system hyperexcitability in stiff-person syndrome
No reported fasciculations, myokymia, muscle cramps, or delayed relaxation
The documented phenotype is classical stiff-person syndrome rather than peripheral nerve hyperexcitability

data.diagnosis: Giant cell arteritis (temporal arteritis) with scalp necrosis
data.description: A large-vessel granulomatous vasculitis affecting cranial branches of the carotid artery, typically in older adults. Severe ischemia of scalp arteries can rarely cause painful ulcers or scalp necrosis.
symptoms_in_common: Scalp ulcer with dark necrotic eschar
Localized scalp ischemic-appearing lesion
Possible involvement of cranial and extracranial arteries on vascular imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Jaw claudication is not described
New headache is not described
Visual loss or diplopia is not described
Polymyalgia rheumatica symptoms are not described
Fever or elevated inflammatory markers are not provided

data.diagnosis: Atherosclerotic carotid or subclavian artery disease causing scalp ischemia
data.description: Atherosclerotic narrowing or occlusion of major cervical arteries can reduce blood flow to the scalp, especially when collateral circulation is limited, and may lead to ischemic skin ulceration.
symptoms_in_common: Vascular imaging appears to show major cervical or proximal arterial narrowing
Focal scalp lesion with necrotic appearance
Evidence compatible with impaired arterial perfusion
symptoms_not_in_common: Typical vascular risk factors such as smoking, diabetes, hypertension, or hyperlipidemia are not described
Transient ischemic attacks or stroke symptoms are not described
Arm claudication or subclavian steal symptoms are not described
Generalized diffuse atherosclerotic symptoms are not described

data.description: A chronic inflammatory large-vessel vasculitis involving the aorta and its major branches. Stenosis of subclavian, carotid, or other arch vessels can produce ischemic manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal large-vessel appearance on angiographic imaging
Potential stenosis involving proximal cervical arteries
Ischemic scalp lesion could occur in severe arterial insufficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Takayasu arteritis usually begins in younger individuals, while patient age is not provided
Limb claudication is not described
Unequal blood pressures or absent pulses are not described
Constitutional symptoms such as fever, fatigue, or weight loss are not described
Scalp necrosis is uncommon in Takayasu arteritis

data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that can cause painful skin nodules, ulcers, livedo reticularis, peripheral neuropathy, and organ ischemia.
symptoms_in_common: Necrotic skin ulceration can occur due to arterial vasculitis
Focal tissue ischemia is compatible with vasculitic arterial involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Livedo reticularis is not described
Painful subcutaneous nodules are not described
Peripheral neuropathy is not described
Renal, abdominal, or testicular symptoms are not described
The demonstrated large-vessel abnormality is less typical than in giant cell arteritis or Takayasu arteritis

data.diagnosis: Visceral leishmaniasis (Mediterranean kala-azar due to Leishmania infantum)
data.description: A systemic protozoal infection caused in Spain most commonly by Leishmania infantum. Amastigotes (Leishman-Donovan bodies) can be seen within macrophages in bone marrow or other reticuloendothelial tissue, and marked polyclonal hypergammaglobulinemia may occur.
symptoms_in_common: Microscopic image consistent with numerous intracellular and extracellular Leishmania amastigotes in a marrow/blood-related specimen
Organisms appearing in clusters within macrophages
Abnormal serum appearance compatible with increased serum globulins/hypergammaglobulinemia
Residence in Spain, an endemic region for Leishmania infantum

data.description: A systemic fungal infection caused by Histoplasma species. Small intracellular yeasts may be found within macrophages and can resemble Leishmania amastigotes on microscopy, especially in bone marrow specimens.
symptoms_in_common: Small intracellular organisms within macrophages on microscopy
Possible systemic reticuloendothelial involvement suggested by a marrow-type smear
symptoms_not_in_common: The organisms shown are more suggestive of Leishmania amastigotes than budding Histoplasma yeasts
Spain is not a typical endemic setting for histoplasmosis without travel exposure
Serum hypergammaglobulinemia is more characteristic of visceral leishmaniasis

data.description: A localized Leishmania infection that usually produces one or more chronic skin ulcers or nodules after sandfly exposure. Amastigotes are usually demonstrated from skin lesions rather than bone marrow.
symptoms_in_common: Leishmania-like amastigotes on microscopy
Residence in Spain, where Leishmania transmission can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Apparent heavy involvement of macrophages in a marrow/blood-related specimen is atypical for localized cutaneous disease
Abnormal serum findings compatible with hypergammaglobulinemia are not typical of isolated cutaneous leishmaniasis
No skin ulcer, nodule, or localized skin lesion is described

data.description: An uncommon inflammatory skin disorder characterized by recurrent cellulitis-like red plaques, sometimes with central vesicles, bullae, crusting, or induration. Biopsy commonly shows dermal eosinophilic inflammation and collagen 'flame figures.'
symptoms_in_common: Large erythematous plaque resembling cellulitis
Central yellow-brown crusted or blistered area
Inflamed, indurated-appearing skin
Histologic appearance compatible with dermal inflammatory infiltrate and altered collagen
symptoms_not_in_common: No recurrent episodes are described
No itch, burning, pain, fever, or peripheral eosinophilia is reported

data.diagnosis: Erythema migrans due to Lyme borreliosis
data.description: An expanding erythematous skin lesion occurring after an Ixodes tick bite and representing early Lyme disease. It may become annular or develop central clearing, although atypical crusted lesions can occur at the bite site.
symptoms_in_common: Expanding-looking erythematous plaque
Annular or target-like red border
Possible central bite-site change or crust
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion has prominent central yellow crusting rather than typical central clearing
No known tick bite is reported
No fever, fatigue, headache, joint pain, or neurologic symptoms are reported

data.description: A localized inflammatory or hypersensitivity reaction after a bite from a tick, mosquito, spider, flea, or other arthropod. It can cause redness, swelling, blistering, excoriation, and crusting.
symptoms_in_common: Localized erythematous plaque
Central crusted lesion compatible with a bite punctum or excoriation
Surrounding inflammatory redness
Possible dermal inflammatory reaction on biopsy
symptoms_not_in_common: No definite insect or tick exposure is described
The lesion appears relatively large for a routine uncomplicated insect bite
No pruritus or acute pain is reported

data.description: A bacterial skin infection, often caused by streptococci or staphylococci, that produces warm, tender expanding erythema. Ecthyma is a deeper crusted bacterial infection that can form a yellow-brown adherent crust.
symptoms_in_common: Red inflammatory plaque
Central yellow-brown crusting
Appearance that can resemble localized cellulitis
symptoms_not_in_common: No pain, warmth, rapidly progressive swelling, pus, or fever is reported
The annular configuration is less typical of routine bacterial cellulitis
Histology as shown is not specifically diagnostic of bacterial infection

data.description: Laboratory results on presentation and during repeat testing showed severe hypocalcemia with low ionized calcium, marked hyperphosphatemia, elevated parathyroid hormone, mild hyperchloremia with mildly increased anion gap, and normal renal function, glucose, magnesium, and albumin. Urine testing showed high sodium, low calcium, and very high phosphorus.

A disorder of parathyroid hormone resistance caused by abnormal methylation at the GNAS locus. The methylation pattern shown, with increased NESP methylation and loss of methylation at other GNAS differentially methylated regions, is characteristic of PHP1B.
symptoms_in_common: Severe hypocalcemia with low ionized calcium
Marked hyperphosphatemia
Elevated parathyroid hormone indicating end-organ resistance to PTH
Normal renal function despite hyperphosphatemia
Low urinary calcium
Abnormal GNAS methylation pattern on testing
symptoms_not_in_common: Very high urinary phosphorus, which may be less typical because renal PTH resistance generally causes impaired phosphate excretion
High urinary sodium, which is not a defining feature of PHP1B
Mildly increased anion gap, which is not a classic feature

data.description: A familial form of PHP1B, often due to maternal genetic or epigenetic defects affecting GNAS methylation, commonly involving STX16-related regulatory regions. It produces renal resistance to PTH without necessarily causing the skeletal features of Albright hereditary osteodystrophy.
symptoms_in_common: Hypocalcemia
Hyperphosphatemia
High PTH concentration
Normal kidney function
Low urinary calcium
GNAS methylation abnormalities
Maternal methylation pattern may be normal despite an inherited regulatory defect
symptoms_not_in_common: Very high urinary phosphorus is not the expected classic renal phosphate-handling pattern
High urinary sodium is nonspecific
No family history or inheritance pattern is provided

data.description: A form of PTH resistance caused by maternally inherited inactivating mutations in GNAS. It is often associated with Albright hereditary osteodystrophy, including short stature, round face, obesity, brachydactyly, and possible resistance to other hormones.
symptoms_in_common: Hypocalcemia
Hyperphosphatemia
Elevated PTH
Normal renal function can be present
Low urinary calcium may occur
symptoms_not_in_common: The reported finding is an abnormal GNAS methylation pattern, whereas PHP1A is usually caused by a coding GNAS mutation rather than a primary methylation defect
No Albright hereditary osteodystrophy features are reported
No evidence of resistance to thyroid-stimulating hormone, gonadotropins, or other hormones is provided
Very high urinary phosphorus is not typical

data.description: A rare form of PTH resistance in which the renal cyclic-AMP response to exogenous PTH is preserved but the phosphaturic response is impaired. It causes hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and secondary elevation of PTH.
symptoms_in_common: Hypocalcemia
Hyperphosphatemia
Elevated PTH
Normal renal function
symptoms_not_in_common: The abnormal GNAS methylation pattern strongly favors PHP1B rather than PHP2
Low urinary calcium is not specifically diagnostic of PHP2
Very high urinary phosphorus is not the usual consequence of impaired PTH-mediated phosphaturia
No PTH infusion test demonstrating preserved urinary cyclic-AMP generation is provided

data.diagnosis: Chronic kidney disease with secondary hyperparathyroidism
data.description: Reduced kidney function causes phosphate retention, low calcitriol production, hypocalcemia, and compensatory elevation of PTH. It is a common cause of the biochemical combination of hypocalcemia, hyperphosphatemia, and high PTH.
symptoms_in_common: Hypocalcemia
Hyperphosphatemia
Elevated PTH
Possible acid-base abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Renal function is reported as normal
The abnormal GNAS methylation result is not explained by chronic kidney disease
Low urinary calcium may occur but is not specific
The presentation is more consistent with PTH resistance than phosphate retention from renal failure

data.description: One month before admission, laboratory values were largely normal except for mild leukopenia and thrombocytopenia. On admission, there was marked lymphopenia, thrombocytopenia, mild coagulopathy with very high D-dimer, acute kidney injury, elevated AST/ALT and bilirubin, elevated alkaline phosphatase and LDH, elevated creatine kinase, and abnormal urinalysis with blood and protein. By hospital day 5, hemoglobin had decreased further, platelets remained low, D-dimer and liver enzymes remained elevated, and creatinine had improved.

Systemic infection with Histoplasma capsulatum, often causing reticuloendothelial involvement of the liver, spleen, bone marrow, and lungs, particularly in immunocompromised patients. Tissue typically shows granulomatous inflammation with small intracellular yeasts highlighted by fungal stains.
symptoms_in_common: Marked lymphopenia
Thrombocytopenia and progressive anemia
Elevated LDH
Elevated AST, ALT, bilirubin, and alkaline phosphatase
Hepatic and splenic imaging abnormalities
Acute kidney injury
Mild coagulopathy with markedly elevated D-dimer
Granulomatous liver inflammation with fungal-appearing organisms on special staining
Pulmonary abnormalities on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent pulmonary cystic or pneumatocelic changes are less typical than diffuse nodules, consolidation, or mediastinal lymphadenopathy
Elevated creatine kinase is not a classic feature

data.description: A systemic protozoal infection caused by Leishmania species, endemic in parts of Spain, characterized by invasion of macrophages in the spleen, liver, and bone marrow and commonly causing pancytopenia, hepatosplenomegaly, and liver dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Leukopenia/marked lymphopenia
Thrombocytopenia
Progressive anemia
Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin
Elevated alkaline phosphatase and LDH
Hepatic and splenic abnormalities
Renal dysfunction
Granulomatous inflammatory changes in liver tissue may occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Pulmonary cystic lesions are unusual in visceral leishmaniasis
Very high D-dimer and coagulopathy are not typical presenting findings
Fungal-stain-positive yeast-like organisms would favor histoplasmosis rather than Leishmania

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with hepatic and splenic involvement
data.description: Miliary or disseminated Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection can involve the liver, spleen, bone marrow, kidneys, and lungs, producing granulomas, cytopenias, cholestatic hepatitis, and systemic inflammatory laboratory abnormalities.

Progressive anemia
Elevated alkaline phosphatase, bilirubin, AST, and ALT
Elevated LDH
Hepatic and splenic lesions
Granulomatous hepatitis on biopsy
Pulmonary imaging abnormalities
Acute kidney injury with hematuria and proteinuria

data.description: Systemic infection with Cryptococcus species, usually in advanced cellular immunodeficiency, which can involve the lungs, bloodstream, central nervous system, liver, spleen, and kidneys. Organisms may be visible in tissue with special fungal stains.
symptoms_in_common: Marked lymphopenia suggesting impaired cellular immunity
Pulmonary CT abnormalities
Liver enzyme elevation and hyperbilirubinemia
Acute kidney injury with urinary blood and protein
Thrombocytopenia and anemia
Possible fungal organisms in tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: Hepatic and splenic granulomatous lesions are less characteristic than in histoplasmosis or tuberculosis
Very high D-dimer and coagulopathy are not typical defining features
No neurologic manifestations or meningitis findings are described

data.diagnosis: Secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) triggered by disseminated infection
data.description: A life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by uncontrolled immune activation, often triggered by infections such as histoplasmosis, leishmaniasis, tuberculosis, or viral infection. It can cause cytopenias, hepatitis, coagulopathy, renal injury, and marked LDH elevation.
symptoms_in_common: Cytopenias involving lymphocytes, platelets, and hemoglobin
Progressive anemia during hospitalization
Elevated liver enzymes and bilirubin
Coagulopathy with very high D-dimer
Elevated LDH
Acute kidney injury
Possible hepatosplenic involvement
Underlying systemic infectious process suggested by pathology and imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Fever, hyperferritinemia, hypertriglyceridemia, hypofibrinogenemia, and hemophagocytosis are not provided
Pulmonary cystic lesions are not a typical direct manifestation of HLH
HLH alone would not explain fungal organisms in liver tissue

data.description: A malignant epithelial ovarian tumor characterized by clear, glycogen-rich cells and often associated with endometriosis. It may present as a pelvic or ovarian mass.
symptoms_in_common: Small pelvic/adnexal mass seen on transvaginal ultrasound
Pelvic mass seen on abdominal MRI
Tumor cells with clear/vacuolated cytoplasm on histology
symptoms_not_in_common: No pelvic pain, abdominal distension, abnormal bleeding, weight loss, or other clinical symptoms were provided

data.diagnosis: Ovarian steroid cell tumor, not otherwise specified

Cells with abundant clear or vacuolated cytoplasm on pathology
symptoms_not_in_common: No virilization, hirsutism, acne, deepening of the voice, menstrual disturbance, or endocrine symptoms were provided

data.description: A fluid-filled cavity (syrinx) within the spinal cord, often in the cervical region. It may be congenital, idiopathic, familial, or secondary to impaired cerebrospinal-fluid flow.

Round central cord cavity on axial MRI

data.diagnosis: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis with hemorrhagic venous infarcts

Areas of diffusion restriction compatible with acute infarction or cytotoxic edema

data.diagnosis: Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (PRES) with hemorrhagic or cytotoxic features

Possible small hemorrhagic susceptibility foci

Multifocal distribution

Spinal cord enlargement/abnormal signal with contrast enhancement
Granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells on histology
Apparent noncaseating granulomas

Residence in Spain, where tuberculosis remains possible

data.description: Severe anemia and thrombocytopenia on admission, with hemoglobin 7.6 g/dl, hematocrit 20.9%, and platelets 36,000/mm3; leukocyte count 6,500/mm3. data.description: Male patient with hypernatremia and hyperchloremia on presentation (Na 164 mmol/L, Cl 124 mmol/L), elevated serum osmolality (334 mOsm/kg), elevated BUN with near-normal creatinine, and mild AST elevation. Endocrine testing showed very low LH, FSH, testosterone, and estradiol, elevated prolactin, low free T4 with non-elevated cortisol and ACTH, and low IGF-1. Lipids were mildly elevated (total cholesterol 232 mg/dL, LDL 154 mg/dL). Over the next 3 days, sodium improved to 160 mmol/L and chloride remained elevated. Admission labs also showed urine sodium 64 mmol/L and urine osmolality 314 mOsm/kg. CSF was clear with mild pleocytosis, elevated protein, normal glucose, and no malignant cells.

Mild CSF pleocytosis and elevated CSF protein can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Mild AST elevation
Mild hypercholesterolemia and elevated LDL
Elevated BUN with near-normal creatinine, which is more likely due to dehydration from diabetes insipidus than the tumor itself

data.description: Granulomatous inflammation from sarcoidosis can infiltrate the hypothalamus, pituitary stalk, pituitary gland, optic pathways, and meninges, producing diabetes insipidus and multiple pituitary hormone deficiencies.
symptoms_in_common: Central diabetes insipidus physiology with hypernatremia, hyperosmolality, and relatively dilute urine
Anterior hypopituitarism with low gonadotropins, sex hormones, free T4, IGF-1, and potentially ACTH-cortisol impairment
Hyperprolactinemia due to interruption of hypothalamic dopamine delivery through the pituitary stalk
Enhancing hypothalamic-pituitary/stalk lesions on MRI
Potential visual-field deficits from optic chiasm or hypothalamic involvement
CSF pleocytosis and elevated protein consistent with inflammatory meningeal involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported pulmonary, lymph-node, skin, eye, or systemic sarcoidosis manifestations
Mild AST elevation is nonspecific
Hyperlipidemia is not a characteristic presenting feature

data.description: Central nervous system tuberculosis can cause chronic basilar meningitis and enhancing granulomas involving the pituitary stalk, hypothalamus, optic chiasm, or adjacent brain structures. Endocrine dysfunction and diabetes insipidus may result.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing intracranial lesions in the suprasellar/hypothalamic region
Central diabetes insipidus pattern causing hypernatremia and high serum osmolality
Multiple anterior pituitary hormone deficiencies
Mild CSF pleocytosis and increased CSF protein
Possible visual impairment or visual-field abnormalities from chiasmal/optic pathway involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: CSF glucose is normal, whereas tuberculous meningitis often lowers CSF glucose
No reported fever, headache, constitutional symptoms, pulmonary tuberculosis history, or known tuberculosis exposure
No reported marked CSF lymphocytosis or microbiologic evidence of tuberculosis

data.diagnosis: Primary central nervous system lymphoma involving the hypothalamus-pituitary region
data.description: Primary CNS lymphoma can present as enhancing periventricular, hypothalamic, or suprasellar lesions. Involvement of the pituitary stalk or hypothalamus can cause diabetes insipidus, hyperprolactinemia, and hypopituitarism.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing hypothalamic/suprasellar lesions on MRI
Possible multifocal intracranial lesions
Central diabetes insipidus with severe hypernatremia and inadequate urinary concentration
Hypopituitarism involving gonadal, thyroid, growth-hormone, and adrenal axes
Hyperprolactinemia from pituitary-stalk dysfunction
Elevated CSF protein and mild CSF pleocytosis can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No malignant cells identified in CSF
No reported immunosuppression, weight loss, fever, or other lymphoma-related systemic symptoms
The endocrine-predominant presentation is less common than focal neurologic deficits or cognitive changes

data.diagnosis: Langerhans cell histiocytosis with hypothalamic-pituitary involvement
data.description: Langerhans cell histiocytosis can infiltrate the posterior pituitary, pituitary stalk, and hypothalamus. Diabetes insipidus is a classic endocrine manifestation, and anterior pituitary deficiencies may develop with more extensive disease.
symptoms_in_common: Central diabetes insipidus causing hypernatremia, hyperosmolality, and relatively low urine osmolality
Pituitary-stalk/hypothalamic abnormalities on MRI
Low gonadotropins and sex hormones consistent with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism
Low free T4, low IGF-1, and possible adrenal-axis impairment
Elevated prolactin due to stalk involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported bone lesions, skin rash, lung disease, lymphadenopathy, or other systemic Langerhans cell histiocytosis findings
Multifocal deep intracranial enhancing lesions are less typical than isolated stalk thickening
CSF pleocytosis and elevated protein are not usual hallmark findings

data.diagnosis: Partial atrioventricular septal defect (ostium primum atrial septal defect)
data.description: A congenital defect of the lower interatrial septum associated with abnormal atrioventricular valve anatomy, often including a cleft in the left atrioventricular (mitral) valve. It commonly causes right-sided volume overload and conduction abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Echocardiographic appearance suggestive of an atrial septal defect near the atrioventricular valves
Possible abnormal atrioventricular valve anatomy on echocardiography
Prolonged PR interval/first-degree atrioventricular block pattern on ECG
Broad or notched P-wave appearance, which may reflect atrial enlargement
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as exertional dyspnea, fatigue, palpitations, recurrent respiratory infections, or edema were provided

data.description: A common congenital opening in the central interatrial septum that allows left-to-right shunting, potentially producing right atrial and right ventricular enlargement and atrial arrhythmias later in life.
symptoms_in_common: Possible interatrial septal defect on echocardiographic images
Possible atrial enlargement suggested by broad/notched P waves
May be asymptomatic until adulthood
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked PR prolongation is less characteristic than in a primum atrial septal defect
No reported fixed split second heart sound, exertional breathlessness, fatigue, palpitations, or right-heart failure symptoms

data.description: A rare congenital anomaly in which a membrane divides the left atrium into two chambers, potentially obstructing pulmonary venous drainage and mimicking mitral stenosis.
symptoms_in_common: Possible left-atrial membrane or partition seen on echocardiographic views
Broad or notched P-wave morphology that can occur with left atrial enlargement
Potential structural left-atrial abnormality on echocardiography
symptoms_not_in_common: Prolonged PR interval is not a typical defining feature
No reported pulmonary congestion, dyspnea, exercise intolerance, hemoptysis, recurrent chest infections, or pulmonary hypertension findings

data.diagnosis: Infantile-onset Pompe disease (glycogen storage disease type II)
data.description: An autosomal-recessive lysosomal storage disorder caused by severe acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) deficiency, resulting in lysosomal glycogen accumulation, especially in cardiac and skeletal muscle. Classic infantile disease causes hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, hypotonia, weakness, and respiratory failure.
symptoms_in_common: Infant chest radiograph with an enlarged cardiac silhouette suggestive of cardiomyopathy
Laboratory image indicating markedly reduced or abnormal processing of GAA protein, including absent or greatly reduced mature GAA enzyme
Presentation in infancy

data.description: A milder form of acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency with residual enzyme activity. It primarily causes progressive proximal skeletal-muscle and respiratory-muscle weakness; clinically significant cardiomyopathy is uncommon.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal GAA protein/enzyme findings consistent with acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency
symptoms_not_in_common: Infant presentation
Chest radiograph appearance suggestive of cardiomegaly or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy

data.description: An X-linked lysosomal/autophagy-related disorder caused by LAMP2 deficiency. It can produce severe hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, skeletal myopathy, and intellectual disability, usually affecting boys.
symptoms_in_common: Possible cardiomyopathy suggested by the enlarged cardiac silhouette on chest radiograph
Potential skeletal-muscle involvement in a lysosomal-related disorder
symptoms_not_in_common: Abnormal acid alpha-glucosidase (GAA) maturation or deficiency is not typical
Classic severe infantile presentation is less typical than in infantile Pompe disease

data.description: Progressive anemia over 1 year: hematocrit 35.6% to 30.9%, hemoglobin 12.0 to 10.6 g/dl, with microcytosis (MCV 75 fL on admission). Earlier leukocytosis and inflammatory markers were elevated, with ESR 41–66 mm/hr and CRP 3.0 to 8.3 mg/dl. On admission, reticulocytes 3.0%, PT 14.4 sec/INR 1.2, LDH 517 U/liter, ferritin 470 ng/ml, platelets 366,000/mm3, and Borrelia antibodies negative.

A malignant proliferation of immature B-lymphoblasts involving bone marrow and potentially extranodal sites. It commonly expresses B-cell markers such as CD19 and often CD10; aberrant myeloid-marker expression such as CD33 can occur.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive anemia
Elevated LDH
Bone marrow infiltrate composed of immature-appearing cells
Flow-cytometric B-cell phenotype with CD19 and CD10 expression
Possible aberrant CD33 expression
Multifocal FDG-avid extranodal lesions on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Slow progression over approximately 1 year is less typical than the usually more rapidly progressive presentation
Microcytosis is not a characteristic feature of B-ALL/LBL
Markedly elevated ESR and CRP are nonspecific and not classic presenting findings

data.description: An aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that may involve lymph nodes, bone marrow, muscle, kidneys, liver, or other extranodal sites and is typically strongly FDG-avid on PET imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Anemia
Elevated LDH
Prior leukocytosis
Elevated inflammatory markers
Multifocal soft-tissue and visceral abnormalities on CT
Multiple FDG-avid lesions on PET/CT
Bone marrow involvement by abnormal B-lineage cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytic anemia is not specifically characteristic of DLBCL
CD10 positivity is present only in a subset of DLBCL cases
A year-long indolent anemia course is less typical for untreated aggressive DLBCL

data.description: A highly aggressive mature germinal-center B-cell neoplasm, usually CD19- and CD10-positive, with frequent extranodal and bone marrow involvement and elevated LDH due to rapid cellular turnover.
symptoms_in_common: CD19-positive and CD10-positive B-cell population
Elevated LDH
Anemia due to possible marrow involvement
Multifocal FDG-avid disease
Possible abdominal and extranodal involvement on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: The relatively modest LDH elevation is less typical than the often markedly elevated LDH in Burkitt lymphoma
One year of progressive anemia is much slower than the usual rapidly progressive clinical course
Microcytosis is not a typical feature
Marked ESR and CRP elevation is nonspecific rather than characteristic

data.description: Follicular lymphoma is an indolent germinal-center B-cell lymphoma commonly expressing CD19 and CD10. Transformation to diffuse large B-cell lymphoma can cause rapidly progressive extranodal, marrow, and PET-avid disease with elevated LDH.
symptoms_in_common: Longer history of progressive anemia
CD19-positive and CD10-positive B-cell phenotype
Bone marrow involvement
Elevated LDH
Multifocal PET-avid disease
Elevated inflammatory markers
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytosis is not specific for follicular lymphoma
The apparent blast-like marrow morphology would be less typical for uncomplicated follicular lymphoma
Extensive extranodal disease would raise concern for transformed rather than indolent follicular lymphoma

data.diagnosis: B-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma with disseminated extranodal involvement
data.description: A precursor B-cell neoplasm that is termed lymphoblastic lymphoma when it predominantly forms tissue masses and acute lymphoblastic leukemia when marrow and blood involvement is substantial. It can involve bone, soft tissues, kidneys, and marrow.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal soft-tissue and visceral lesions on CT and PET
Anemia
Elevated LDH
Immature-cell morphology in the marrow sample
CD19 and CD10 expression by the abnormal population
Potential aberrant expression of CD33
symptoms_not_in_common: Microcytosis is not characteristic
A prolonged one-year course is less typical than the usual subacute or rapidly progressive presentation
Elevated ESR and CRP are nonspecific findings

data.description: An acute bacterial infection of the skin and subcutaneous tissue of the breast, causing localized inflammation; ultrasound may show skin thickening and edematous subcutaneous tissue without a drainable abscess.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral diffuse breast erythema
Breast swelling
Inflammatory appearance of the skin and subcutaneous tissues
Ultrasound appearance consistent with subcutaneous edema
No obvious discrete fluid collection on the provided ultrasound image

data.description: A superficial bacterial skin infection, usually caused by streptococci, characterized by rapidly developing red, warm, swollen skin; the borders may be relatively sharp.
symptoms_in_common: Marked localized erythema of the breast
Swelling
Superficial inflammatory skin changes
Unilateral involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: A sharply demarcated raised border is not clearly visible in the images

data.description: An aggressive form of breast cancer in which tumor emboli obstruct dermal lymphatic vessels, producing rapid breast redness, swelling, edema, and sometimes peau d'orange changes. It can mimic mastitis or cellulitis.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse unilateral breast erythema
Breast enlargement or swelling
Edematous skin/subcutaneous tissue appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: No definite breast mass is visible in the provided images
No clear peau d'orange skin texture is visible
The images appear more suggestive of acute superficial inflammation than malignancy

data.description: A localized collection of pus within breast tissue, often developing as a complication of mastitis; it commonly causes focal painful swelling, redness, and a fluctuant mass.
symptoms_in_common: Breast erythema
Localized swelling
Inflammatory changes in surrounding tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: No clear focal fluid collection or drainable abscess cavity is visible on the ultrasound image
No focal fluctuant mass is evident from the photographs

data.description: A chronic inflammatory breast disorder that can produce painful breast swelling, erythema, masses, sinus tracts, or abscess-like lesions and may resemble infection or inflammatory breast cancer.
symptoms_in_common: Unilateral breast redness
Breast swelling
Inflammatory breast appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: No discrete inflammatory mass is apparent
No skin ulceration, fistula, or draining sinus is visible
The ultrasound does not clearly show the typical focal irregular inflammatory lesions

data.description: An inflammatory autoimmune myopathy characterized by distinctive photosensitive skin eruptions and, often, proximal muscle weakness.
symptoms_in_common: Facial erythema
Photosensitive-appearing erythematous rash over the upper chest (V-sign/shawl distribution)
Papular erythematous lesions on the backs of the hands that may resemble Gottron papules
Symmetric involvement of exposed skin areas
symptoms_not_in_common: Muscle weakness is not described
Heliotrope discoloration of the eyelids is not clearly visible

data.description: A photosensitive autoimmune skin manifestation of lupus that commonly causes widespread red, scaly, annular, or papulosquamous lesions on sun-exposed areas.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous facial eruption
Rash on sun-exposed upper chest
Rash on the dorsal hands
Relatively symmetric distribution
symptoms_not_in_common: Typical annular or markedly scaly plaques are not clearly visible
Systemic lupus features such as joint pain, oral ulcers, fever, or renal symptoms are not described

data.description: A delayed abnormal inflammatory reaction to ultraviolet light, producing itchy papules or plaques on newly sun-exposed skin.
symptoms_in_common: Papular erythematous eruption on the upper chest
Involvement of sun-exposed dorsal hands
Residence in Spain, where substantial ultraviolet exposure may be relevant
symptoms_not_in_common: Facial involvement is less typical because the face is often chronically sun-adapted
Itch and a clear temporal relationship to sun exposure are not described

data.description: A light-induced skin reaction triggered by ultraviolet exposure together with medications, fragrances, sunscreens, plants, or other topical/systemic agents.
symptoms_in_common: Erythema affecting exposed face, upper chest, and hands
Possible photo-distributed pattern
Papular or eczematous-appearing lesions
symptoms_not_in_common: A medication, fragrance, sunscreen, plant, or other exposure trigger is not provided
Vesicles, marked eczema, burning, or itching are not described

data.description: The disseminated stage of Treponema pallidum infection, which can produce a generalized papular rash and many variable skin findings.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse papular rash involving trunk
Lesions involving the hands
Facial lesions can occur in secondary syphilis
symptoms_not_in_common: Palmar and plantar involvement is not visible
