The eruption appears more photo-distributed than the typical generalized syphilitic rash

data.description: Keratoacanthomas are rapidly growing crateriform keratinizing skin tumors, often considered within the well-differentiated cutaneous squamous-cell carcinoma spectrum. In this case, repeated trauma or surgical excisions may have induced new lesions through an isomorphic (Koebner-like) response.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple papules and nodules on the upper extremity
Crateriform lesions with central keratin and ulceration
Histology reported 15 keratoacanthomas
Development of new lesions after excisions, consistent with an isomorphic response
Progressive localized course
Partial improvement with topical imiquimod and 5-fluorouracil
symptoms_not_in_common: Coexisting verruca vulgaris lesions are not a defining feature of keratoacanthoma
The unusually high number of clustered lesions is less typical than solitary keratoacanthoma

data.description: A rare inherited or sporadic keratoacanthoma syndrome characterized by recurrent multiple keratoacanthoma-like squamous tumors that may involute and leave scars. Lesions can be precipitated by trauma and may occur on sun-exposed limbs.
symptoms_in_common: Numerous keratoacanthoma-like tumors
Histologic diagnosis of keratoacanthoma
Lesions concentrated on an extremity
Scarring after lesions and treatment
Possible trauma-associated emergence of additional lesions
No evidence of metastatic disease on computed tomography
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported family history or early-life recurrent disease
The lesions showed progressive persistence rather than clear spontaneous complete regression
Coexisting common warts are not characteristic

data.description: A very rare disorder involving the sudden appearance of many small keratoacanthomas, often numbering in the hundreds or thousands, typically involving widespread skin and sometimes mucosal sites.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple keratoacanthomas
Papules and nodules with central keratinization
Progressive development of additional lesions
Histologic keratoacanthomas
symptoms_not_in_common: Disease is localized mainly to one upper extremity rather than generalized
Only dozens rather than hundreds to thousands of lesions are described
No facial, mucosal, or widespread body involvement is reported
No reported severe pruritus, ectropion, or mask-like facial changes

data.description: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma is a malignant keratinocyte tumor that may present as a rapidly growing hyperkeratotic, ulcerated, crateriform nodule. Keratoacanthoma-type lesions can be difficult to distinguish histologically and clinically from conventional keratoacanthoma.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcerated and crusted keratinizing nodules
Lesions on a sun-exposed upper extremity
Progressive lesions despite an initial period without therapy
Keratoacanthoma histology, which lies in the squamous neoplasia spectrum
Response to topical antineoplastic therapies such as 5-fluorouracil and imiquimod
symptoms_not_in_common: The multiplicity and apparent isomorphic response are more suggestive of a keratoacanthoma syndrome than sporadic squamous cell carcinoma
No metastases or lymphadenopathy were detected
Some biopsies showed verruca vulgaris rather than carcinoma

data.diagnosis: Verruca vulgaris (common warts) with secondary irritation or ulceration
data.description: Common warts are human papillomavirus-associated benign epidermal proliferations, usually presenting as rough hyperkeratotic papules. They can coexist with or mimic keratoacanthomatous lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Histology documented 3 verruca vulgaris lesions
Multiple papules on the hand and forearm
Hyperkeratotic and crusted surface changes
Potential response to imiquimod and 5-fluorouracil
symptoms_not_in_common: Most biopsied lesions were keratoacanthomas rather than warts
Large crateriform ulcerated tumors are not typical of ordinary warts
Rapid progressive tumor-like growth and marked scarring are atypical for uncomplicated verruca vulgaris

data.description: A chronic immune-mediated demyelinating disorder of the central nervous system that commonly produces short-segment, patchy spinal cord lesions, often in the cervical and thoracic cord.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple focal intramedullary T2-hyperintense spinal cord lesions in the cervical and thoracic regions
Lesions appear relatively short in length and peripheral/dorsal within the cord, a pattern compatible with multiple sclerosis

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory disorder, often associated with aquaporin-4 antibodies, causing severe optic neuritis and myelitis; spinal lesions are typically longitudinally extensive.
symptoms_in_common: Intramedullary spinal cord signal abnormalities on T2-weighted MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: The visible lesions appear focal and short-segment rather than extending continuously through three or more vertebral segments
No optic neuritis, severe myelitis symptoms, vomiting, or area-postrema symptoms were provided

data.description: An autoimmune demyelinating disease that can cause optic neuritis, acute myelitis, and brain or spinal cord lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Spinal cord T2-signal lesions may occur in the cervical and thoracic spinal cord
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute transverse myelitis symptoms were provided

The lesions do not clearly show the long, central cord involvement often seen in this condition

data.description: Spinal cord dysfunction caused by degenerative cervical disc disease, osteophytes, or spinal canal narrowing with chronic cord compression.

A separate thoracic cord lesion would be atypical for a purely cervical degenerative process

data.diagnosis: T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia/lymphoma (T-ALL/LBL) with t(X;14)(q22.3;q11.2) involving IRS4 and TCRA/D
data.description: An aggressive precursor T-lymphoid neoplasm characterized by marrow and peripheral-blood infiltration by lymphoblasts. The images show an X;14 rearrangement involving the T-cell receptor alpha/delta locus on chromosome 14 and the IRS4 region on Xq22.3, a rare abnormality associated with T-ALL.

Bone marrow extensively infiltrated by immature lymphoid blasts
Cytogenetic evidence of t(X;14) involving chromosome 14 TCRA/D region
Marked replacement of normal marrow hematopoietic cells by blasts

No immunophenotyping results confirming T-cell lineage were provided

data.diagnosis: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia of ambiguous or initially unclassified lineage
data.description: Acute lymphoblastic leukemia is a malignancy of immature lymphoid precursor cells that can heavily involve blood and bone marrow. Definitive lineage assignment requires flow-cytometric immunophenotyping and molecular testing.

Hypercellular marrow with diffuse blast infiltration
Suppression or displacement of normal marrow elements
symptoms_not_in_common: The TCRA/D-associated chromosome 14 rearrangement strongly favors T-lineage rather than unclassified ALL

data.description: A malignant proliferation of immature B-lymphoid precursor cells that commonly presents with marrow failure and circulating blasts. It can appear morphologically similar to T-ALL but usually has distinct B-cell immunophenotypic and genetic findings.

Bone marrow diffusely infiltrated by acute leukemia blasts
Loss of normal marrow architecture due to blast replacement
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent rearrangement involving the TCRA/D locus on chromosome 14 is not typical of B-ALL and favors T-ALL

Systemic infection by Leishmania parasites, usually transmitted by sandflies. It causes reticuloendothelial involvement with fever, hepatosplenomegaly, marrow suppression, and pancytopenia. Intracellular amastigotes may be seen within macrophages on peripheral-blood or bone-marrow examination.

Severe anemia (hemoglobin 78 g/L)
Thrombocytopenia (platelet count 41 x 10^9/L)
Pancytopenia
Imaging compatible with splenomegaly and possible hepatomegaly
Macrophages containing structures compatible with intracellular Leishmania amastigotes on smear images
Tissue histology showing diffuse macrophage/histiocyte infiltration
symptoms_not_in_common: Extremely high ferritin (375,554 ng/mL), which is more suggestive of secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis
Hypofibrinogenemia
Extensive bilateral pulmonary consolidation/infiltrates, which is not a classic primary manifestation of visceral leishmaniasis

data.diagnosis: Secondary hemophagocytic lymphohistiocytosis (HLH) triggered by visceral leishmaniasis
data.description: A life-threatening hyperinflammatory syndrome caused by uncontrolled immune activation, often triggered by infections such as visceral leishmaniasis. Typical findings include fever, cytopenias, hypofibrinogenemia, very high ferritin, splenomegaly, and hemophagocytosis in marrow or other tissues.
symptoms_in_common: Pancytopenia
Leukopenia (white blood cell count 1.25 x 10^9/L)
Anemia (hemoglobin 78 g/L)
Thrombocytopenia (platelet count 41 x 10^9/L)
Hypofibrinogenemia (fibrinogen 1.79 g/L)
Extreme hyperferritinemia (375,554 ng/mL)
Splenomegaly suggested by abdominal imaging
Histologic appearance compatible with activated macrophages and possible hemophagocytosis
Potential infectious trigger from intracellular Leishmania-like organisms
symptoms_not_in_common: Intracellular amastigotes are not caused by HLH itself; they indicate the underlying infectious trigger
Bilateral pulmonary infiltrates are possible in severe HLH but are not a defining diagnostic feature

data.diagnosis: Severe disseminated visceral leishmaniasis with pulmonary involvement
data.description: An advanced form of visceral leishmaniasis in which widespread infection and immune dysregulation can involve the lungs in addition to the liver, spleen, and bone marrow. It may coexist with HLH and cause respiratory imaging abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral diffuse pulmonary consolidation or infiltrative changes on chest CT
Pancytopenia
Marked anemia
Leukopenia
Thrombocytopenia
Hepatosplenic involvement on abdominal imaging
Smear findings compatible with intracellular Leishmania organisms in macrophages
Histologic macrophage-rich infiltrates
symptoms_not_in_common: Extreme ferritin elevation is more characteristic of associated HLH than uncomplicated pulmonary leishmaniasis
Low fibrinogen is more characteristic of HLH, severe systemic inflammation, or consumptive coagulopathy than isolated pulmonary infection

data.description: After cardiac arrest and transfer, laboratory studies showed leukocytosis (WBC 19,500/µL with neutrophilia), anemia (hemoglobin 9.6 g/dL, hematocrit 28.2%), hypoalbuminemia (1.9 g/dL), hypoproteinemia (3.6 g/dL), hypocalcemia (total calcium 6.7 mg/dL, ionized calcium 0.96 mmol/L), hyperglycemia (202 mg/dL), markedly elevated AST (648 U/L) and ALT (101 U/L), elevated alkaline phosphatase (132 U/L), prolonged PT (15.0 s) and PTT (>150 s), and markedly elevated troponin T (28.32 ng/mL), creatine kinase (11,012 U/L), and CK-MB (552 U/L). Arterial blood gas on arrival showed pH 7.31 with adequate oxygenation on 100% FiO2.
Transient acute left-ventricular systolic dysfunction, often triggered by major physical or emotional stress, which can mimic acute myocardial infarction despite unobstructed coronary arteries.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac arrest
Marked troponin T, CK, and CK-MB elevation
Electrocardiographic ischemic-appearing ST-T abnormalities
Apparent acute ventricular dysfunction on echocardiography
Coronary angiography without an obstructive coronary lesion
Pulmonary congestion and bilateral pleural effusions on chest imaging
Leukocytosis and hyperglycemia during severe physiologic stress
symptoms_not_in_common: Very marked creatine kinase elevation may also reflect prolonged resuscitation or rhabdomyolysis rather than Takotsubo syndrome alone
Severe prolonged PTT is not a characteristic finding unless related to anticoagulation
Profound hypoalbuminemia and hypoproteinemia are not typical primary features
Marked AST elevation is more suggestive of ischemic hepatitis or muscle injury after arrest

data.description: A benign inflammatory skin condition causing smooth annular plaques formed by grouped papules, usually without scale.
symptoms_in_common: Smooth, non-scaly annular lesions
Red-brown coloration
Absence of reported systemic symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesions appear more like expanding erythematous patches than firm papular rings
The trunk distribution and multiple target-like lesions are less typical
No chronicity or slow progression was reported

data.diagnosis: Infectious aortitis with mycotic abdominal aortic pseudoaneurysm
data.description: Infection of the aortic wall can cause inflammation, wall destruction, and a rapidly enlarging saccular pseudoaneurysm. Potential pathogens in Spain include Salmonella species, Staphylococcus aureus, Coxiella burnetii, and Brucella species.
symptoms_in_common: Serial CT appearances suggesting progressive focal abnormality of the abdominal aortic wall
Focal saccular outpouching/pseudoaneurysm adjacent to the abdominal aorta
Periaortic soft-tissue inflammatory change
Apparent increase in size of the vascular lesion over time
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, chills, bacteremia, abdominal pain, back pain, or constitutional symptoms were provided
Marked gastric distension is not a typical primary feature of aortic infection

data.diagnosis: Abdominal aortic intramural hematoma or penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer
data.description: An intramural hematoma is bleeding within the aortic wall, while a penetrating atherosclerotic ulcer is an ulcerated atherosclerotic plaque that extends into the media. Either can progress to focal pseudoaneurysm or rupture.
symptoms_in_common: Focal abnormal thickening of the abdominal aortic wall
Possible ulcer-like focal defect in the aortic wall
Progression to a focal saccular aneurysmal or pseudoaneurysmal appearance
Periaortic inflammatory-appearing soft tissue may occur with a complicated lesion
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute severe abdominal, flank, or back pain was reported
No hypertension or known atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease was provided
Marked inflammatory periaortic tissue and rapid pseudoaneurysm formation may favor infection over uncomplicated atherosclerotic ulcer disease

data.diagnosis: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm / chronic periaortitis
data.description: Inflammatory abdominal aortic aneurysm is an aneurysm associated with dense periaortic inflammation and fibrosis. It can overlap with IgG4-related disease and may cause pain or obstruction of nearby structures.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal abdominal aortic enlargement or focal aneurysmal change
Periaortic soft-tissue thickening/inflammatory rind
Possible involvement of adjacent retroperitoneal structures
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears focal and pseudoaneurysmal rather than a typical fusiform infrarenal abdominal aortic aneurysm
No chronic abdominal or back pain was provided
No ureteral obstruction, hydronephrosis, elevated inflammatory markers, or other IgG4-related manifestations were reported

data.diagnosis: Gastrocolic fistula involving the gastric pouch and transverse colon
data.description: An abnormal communication between the stomach (in this case the gastric pouch) and the colon. The contrast study directly demonstrates passage between the gastric pouch and transverse colon.
symptoms_in_common: Endoscopic appearance of an abnormal opening in the gastric pouch
Contrast radiographic demonstration of a fistulous tract from the gastric pouch to the transverse colon

data.description: A gastrocolic fistula can occur as a late complication of bariatric surgery, particularly after Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, often related to marginal ulceration, staple-line problems, or local inflammation.
symptoms_in_common: Fistula arising from a gastric pouch
Communication between the gastric pouch and transverse colon on contrast imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of bariatric surgery was explicitly provided
No reported diarrhea, feculent vomiting, abdominal pain, or weight loss

data.diagnosis: Marginal ulcer with fistulization to the colon
data.description: A marginal ulcer is an ulcer near a gastrojejunal anastomosis or gastric pouch after gastric surgery. Deep ulceration and inflammation can rarely erode into adjacent colon and form a gastrocolic fistula.
symptoms_in_common: Gastric pouch fistulous opening
Gastrocolic communication that could result from ulcer erosion
symptoms_not_in_common: No ulcer crater or active bleeding is explicitly described
No reported epigastric pain, nausea, gastrointestinal bleeding, or anemia

data.diagnosis: Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), likely chronic bronchitis phenotype
data.description: A chronic airflow-limiting lung disease, commonly associated with smoking or environmental exposures. Chest radiographs may show hyperinflation and increased bronchovascular/peribronchial markings.
symptoms_in_common: Mildly hyperinflated-appearing lungs on chest radiograph
Prominent bilateral perihilar/basal bronchovascular or peribronchial markings
No focal acute lung consolidation
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical respiratory symptoms, smoking history, or exposure history were provided
No clear bullous emphysema is visible
No marked diaphragmatic flattening is visible

data.description: A chronic inflammatory airway disorder causing episodic, usually reversible airway obstruction. Chest radiographs can be normal or show mild hyperinflation and peribronchial thickening.
symptoms_in_common: Mild hyperinflation appearance
Possible peribronchial thickening/prominent central bronchial markings
No pleural effusion or focal pneumonia visible
symptoms_not_in_common: No wheezing, episodic shortness of breath, cough, or trigger history was provided
No acute severe air trapping is clearly demonstrated
No clinical history of reversible airway symptoms was provided

data.description: Inflammation of the bronchi, often caused by viral infection, irritant exposure, or smoking. Radiographs may show increased peribronchial markings but often do not show a focal infiltrate.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent bilateral central and lower-lung bronchovascular/peribronchial markings
No focal lobar consolidation
No pleural effusion
symptoms_not_in_common: No cough, sputum production, fever, or chest discomfort was provided
No definite acute inflammatory infiltrate is visible
No laboratory evidence of infection was provided

data.description: A nutritional deficiency disorder caused by inadequate niacin or tryptophan. It can cause photosensitive dermatitis, classically involving the neck (Casal necklace) and sun-exposed hands and forearms.
symptoms_in_common: Symmetric rash on sun-exposed forearms and hands
Erythematous to dusky, thickened skin over the hands and wrists
Excoriated/scaly papules on the forearms
Well-demarcated erythematous, scaly rash around the neck resembling a Casal necklace

data.description: An inflammatory skin reaction triggered or worsened by ultraviolet exposure, sometimes after contact with medications, fragrances, plants, or sunscreens.
symptoms_in_common: Dermatitis affecting exposed forearms and hands
Redness and scaling in the neck and upper chest area
Symmetric distribution of lesions in potentially sun-exposed sites
Excoriations that may occur with itch
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked darkening and thickened appearance of the dorsal hands may be more suggestive of chronic nutritional or photosensitivity-related disease than simple acute photodermatitis

data.description: An autoimmune inflammatory disorder affecting skin and muscle. Characteristic cutaneous features include photosensitive rashes of the neck and upper chest and papules over the knuckles.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous rash over the neck and upper chest in a photosensitive distribution
Rash involving the dorsal hands and wrists
Possible papular lesions on the hands/forearms
Symmetric skin involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No muscle weakness is described
No heliotrope eyelid rash is described
The extensive rough, excoriated forearm lesions are less specific for dermatomyositis

data.diagnosis: Chronic eczematous dermatitis (atopic or contact dermatitis)
data.description: A common inflammatory skin condition characterized by itching, redness, scaling, excoriations, and skin thickening; it may be caused by atopy, irritants, or allergens.
symptoms_in_common: Erythematous scaly plaques on the neck
Excoriated papules and plaques on the forearms
Possible skin thickening and chronic inflammation on the hands
Symmetric involvement of the wrists and forearms
symptoms_not_in_common: The sharply neck-centered and sun-exposed distribution may suggest a photosensitive condition rather than ordinary eczema
Dusky discoloration of the hands is not a classic feature of uncomplicated eczema

data.description: Paciente de 8 meses con anomalías inmunológicas: leucocitos 10,79 ×10^9/L, neutrófilos 19,6%, linfocitos 55,1%, células T CD3+ 89,97%, CD4+ 55,95%, CD8+ 31,82%, CD19+ 11%, CD56+CD16+ 5,78%, IgG bajo (135 mg/dL), IgA muy bajo (<10 mg/dL) e IgM bajo (12 mg/dL). Las pruebas genéticas mostraron mutación BTK c.494G>A (p.C165Y).

data.diagnosis: Agmaglobulinemia ligada al cromosoma X (XLA; Agammaglobulinemia de Bruton)
data.description: Una inmunodeficiencia primaria causada por variantes patógenas de BTK que dificultan la maduración de las células B, resultando en una reducción notable de inmunoglobulinas y susceptibilidad a infecciones bacterianas y enterovirales recurrentes tras el deterioro de los anticuerpos maternos.
symptoms_in_common: Mutación hemicigoto BTK c.494G>A (p.C165Y)
Hipogammaglobulinemia marcada: IgG 135 mg/dL, IgA <10 mg/dL e IgM 12 mg/dL
Edad de 8 meses, cuando la transferencia materna de IgG está disminuyendo y el XLA puede hacerse evidente
Hallazgos de expresión proteica BTK consistentes con un alelo BTK anormal en el paciente
Compartimento predominantemente preservado de células T (células CD3+, CD4+ y CD8+)
Compartimento de células B bajo/limitado en relación con la población total de linfocitos (CD19+ 11%)
symptoms_not_in_common: No se describen infecciones sinopulmonares, gastrointestinales ni bacterianas invasivas recurrentes
Las células B CD19+ son detectables al 11%; la XLA clásica suele presentar células B circulantes profundamente reducidas o casi ausentes

data.diagnosis: Agammaglobulinemia ligada al cromosoma X relacionada con BTK debido al mosaicismo somático/gonadal materno
data.description: Agammaglobulinemia ligada al cromosoma X en un niño varón causada por una variante patogénica BTK heredada de una madre con mosaicismo somático de bajo nivel; el mosaicismo también puede implicar posible afectación de la línea germinal y riesgo de recurrencia.
symptoms_in_common: El paciente tiene la variante patogénica BTK c.494G>A (p.C165Y)
La madre tiene lecturas de baja dosis de la variante c.494G>A en múltiples tejidos: sangre, hisopo bucal, orina y hisopo vaginal
Las fracciones alelísticas variantes en los tejidos maternos son bajas pero detectables, lo que favorece el mosaicismo somático
Las células B maternas muestran una distribución de expresión BTK compatible con el estado de portador mosaico
El paciente presenta una reducción severa de IgG, IgA e IgM, compatible con la disfunción BTK
symptoms_not_in_common: No hay infecciones recurrentes ni complicaciones documentadas en el bebé
El grado exacto de mosaicismo germinal materno no puede determinarse únicamente a partir de la secuenciación tisular reportada

data.description: Un trastorno heterogéneo de deficiencia de anticuerpos caracterizado por una reducción de IgG con bajas IgA y/o IgM y respuestas de anticuerpos deterioradas, que a menudo se presenta con infecciones respiratorias y gastrointestinales recurrentes; generalmente se diagnostica más tarde en la infancia o la edad adulta.
symptoms_in_common: IgG bajo
IgA muy bajo
IgM bajo
Células B CD19+ detectables
symptoms_not_in_common: La presentación a los 8 meses es mucho antes que en un CVID típico
Una mutación patogénica BTK favorece fuertemente la agammaglobulinemia ligada al cromosoma X en lugar de la CVID
No se han reportado infecciones recurrentes, respuestas deficientes a la vacuna, autoinmunidad, linfadenopatía ni esplenomegalia
El CVID no suele mostrar el característico defecto de maduración de las células B relacionado con BTK

data.description: Un retraso temporal en la maduración de la producción de inmunoglobulinas durante la infancia, que suele implicar bajos niveles de IgG y, a veces, bajos de IgA o IgM, con eventual normalización espontánea.
symptoms_in_common: Edad infantil
IgG bajo
En casos más pronunciados, la IgA y la IgM bajas pueden darse
Células B circulantes detectables
symptoms_not_in_common: La mutación patógena BTK c.494G>A (p.C165Y) no se explica por THI
La reducción profunda de todas las principales clases de inmunoglobulinas es más consistente con XLA
Las anomalías en la expresión proteica BTK no son una característica de THI
La THI es un diagnóstico de exclusión y no puede explicar los hallazgos moleculares

data.diagnosis: Penile fracture (rupture of the right corpus cavernosum tunica albuginea)
data.description: An acute tear of the tunica albuginea surrounding an erect corpus cavernosum, usually caused by blunt bending trauma to the erect penis, with associated hemorrhage.
symptoms_in_common: MRI-visible defect in the tunica albuginea of the right corpus cavernosum near the penile base
Soft-tissue hematoma adjacent to the corporal bodies
Hematoma extending into the right scrotal sac
Scrotal hematoma on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical history of a popping sound during erection is provided
No penile pain, immediate detumescence, swelling, bruising, or deformity is described
No urinary symptoms or urethral bleeding are reported

data.diagnosis: Penile soft-tissue hematoma due to traumatic corporal injury
data.description: A collection of blood in penile and/or scrotal soft tissues after trauma; it may accompany a penile fracture or occur with less severe soft-tissue injury.
symptoms_in_common: Soft-tissue hematoma at the base of the penis
Right-sided hematoma extending into the scrotum
Scrotal hematoma demonstrated on ultrasound
symptoms_not_in_common: A definite tunica albuginea defect suggests a more specific underlying penile fracture rather than an isolated superficial hematoma
No reported swelling, skin discoloration, pain, or trauma history

data.description: Traumatic injury to erectile tissue of a corpus cavernosum, potentially causing localized bleeding and hematoma; if the tunica albuginea is disrupted, it is classified as penile fracture.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormality involving the right corpus cavernosum
Localized hemorrhagic soft-tissue changes
Extension of hemorrhage into adjacent scrotal tissues
symptoms_not_in_common: The identified tunica albuginea tear favors penile fracture rather than a contained isolated cavernosal contusion
No description of erectile dysfunction, pain, penile curvature, or external bruising

data.description: Datos genéticos de profundidad de lectura para chr1:46654381–46663503 muestran proporciones variables Paciente1/control, sin lecturas alineadas en los exones 18–19 (chr1:46656382–46656466 y chr1:46656135–46656199) y proporciones reducidas en varios otros exones.

Una distrofia muscular congénita autosómica-recesiva causada por variantes patógenas en POMGNT1, que afecta la glicosilación alfa-destroglicano. Comúnmente causa malformaciones cerebrales, anomalías oculares y afectación muscular. POMGNT1 se localiza en la región del cromosoma 1 reportada, y la ausencia o reducción de la cobertura de exones es compatible con una posible deleción de exones.
symptoms_in_common: La ausencia de secuenciación alineada se indica en los exones 18-19 y la cobertura reducida en otros exones dentro de la región del cromosoma 1 que contiene POMGNT1
Ventriculomegalia/hidrocefalia marcada en una resonancia magnética cerebral
Aspecto anormal de sustancia blanca cerebral cerebral y cortical/desarrollo cerebral en la resonancia magnética
Anomalía de imagen oftalmológica sugestiva de afectación estructural del ojo
symptoms_not_in_common: No se reporta debilidad muscular ni hipotonía congénita
No se ha reportado un nivel elevado de creatina quinasa
No se informa de retraso en el desarrollo ni discapacidad intelectual
No se han notificado convulsiones

data.description: Una distrofalopatía congénita grave, generalmente debida a defectos en genes implicados en la glicosilación alfa-destroglicana, incluyendo POMGNT1. Se caracteriza por distrofia muscular congénita, malformaciones cerebrales severas, hidrocefalia y grandes anomalías oculares.
symptoms_in_common: Ventriculomegalia/hidrocefalia grave en una resonancia magnética
Desarrollo cerebral anormal/apariencia de la sustancia blanca en la resonancia magnética
Hallazgos de imagen ocular compatibles con una anomalía ocular estructural congénita
Posible deleción patógena que afecta a POMGNT1, un gen que puede causar un fenotipo del espectro de Walker-Warburg
symptoms_not_in_common: La lissencefalia de adoquines no está claramente documentada en las imágenes de la resonancia magnética proporcionadas
La hipoplasia cerebelosa o hipoplasia del tronco encefálico no está claramente informada
No se ha reportado distrofia muscular congénita
No se ha reportado hipotonía neonatal profunda
No se han notificado convulsiones

data.diagnosis: Distrofia-dicoglicanopatía muscular congénita relacionada con POMGNT1, tipo A3
data.description: Una disgustanopatía grave asociada a POMGNT1 caracterizada por anomalías estructurales cerebrales, hidrocefalia o ventricularomegalia, anomalías oculares y distrofia muscular congénita. Esta categoría incluye el extremo grave del espectro de la enfermedad POMGNT1.
symptoms_in_common: Posible deleción multi-exón o anomalía del número de copia que implica POMGNT1
Agrandamiento ventricular en la resonancia magnética
Apariencia cerebral anormal difusa compatible con un trastorno cerebral del desarrollo
Posibles anomalías estructurales oculares
symptoms_not_in_common: No se describe la debilidad muscular congénita
No se describe el deterioro de alimentación o respiratorio
No se describen las contracturas articulares
No se describe un deterioro del desarrollo marcado

data.diagnosis: Distrofia y distrombopatía muscular de cintura articular relacionada con POMGNT1, tipo C3
data.description: Una distoglicanopatía relacionada con POMGNT1 más leve que puede presentarse con debilidad muscular de la cintura membre, discapacidad intelectual variable y anomalías cerebrales y oculares menos graves o ausentes en comparación con la enfermedad músculo-ojo-cerebro.
symptoms_in_common: Posible deleción/anomalía del número de copias que cause la enfermedad y afecta a POMGNT1
symptoms_not_in_common: La ventralberga/hidrocefalia severa es menos típica de este fenotipo más leve
La aparente anomalía estructural ocular es menos típica
No se ha reportado debilidad de la cintura de los miembros
No se informa de intolerancia al ejercicio
No se ha reportado hipertrofia en la pantorrilla
No se ha reportado un nivel elevado de creatina quinasa

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor arising from prostatic glandular cells; it commonly forms infiltrative small glands and can be supported by prostate-marker immunostaining such as PSA, PSAP, or NKX3.1.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic/prostatic mass seen on CT imaging
Gland-forming malignant cells on cytology
Adenocarcinoma-type glands on tissue histology
Immunohistochemical staining pattern suggestive of prostatic epithelial differentiation
symptoms_not_in_common: No urinary obstruction symptoms were provided
No dysuria was provided
No hematuria was provided
No bone pain was provided
No weight loss or constitutional symptoms were provided

data.diagnosis: Urothelial carcinoma of the bladder or prostatic urethra with glandular differentiation
data.description: A malignant tumor arising from the urothelial lining of the bladder or urethra. Some tumors show glandular differentiation and can involve the prostate or present as a pelvic mass.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic mass near the bladder/prostate region on imaging
Malignant cells identified on cytologic material
Possible glandular features in the sampled tumor
symptoms_not_in_common: The histology appears more gland-forming than typical conventional urothelial carcinoma
No gross or microscopic hematuria was provided
No irritative urinary symptoms were provided
No smoking history or urothelial-cancer risk factors were provided
No flank pain or urinary tract obstruction symptoms were provided

data.diagnosis: Colorectal adenocarcinoma with pelvic extension or invasion of the prostate
data.description: A gland-forming malignant tumor of the colon or rectum that can invade adjacent pelvic structures, including the prostate, seminal vesicles, bladder, or pelvic soft tissues.
symptoms_in_common: Pelvic mass on CT imaging
Adenocarcinoma morphology with malignant glands on histology
Location in the pelvis near bowel and genitourinary structures
symptoms_not_in_common: No rectal bleeding was provided
No change in bowel habits was provided
No abdominal pain was provided
No unexplained anemia was provided
No weight loss was provided
The apparent prostatic localization and prostate-marker staining would be less typical for colorectal primary cancer

data.description: Admission labs showed acidemia with low bicarbonate and low PaCO2, markedly elevated lactate, increased anion gap and osmolality gap, hyperchloremia, mild hyperglycemia, and mildly elevated creatinine; hemoglobin, white cell count, and platelets were within normal limits.

Toxic alcohol ingestion causing high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, an elevated osmolality gap early after exposure, and possible acute kidney injury due to toxic metabolites and calcium oxalate deposition.
symptoms_in_common: Acidemia
Low bicarbonate
Low PaCO2 consistent with respiratory compensation
Markedly elevated lactate or possible falsely elevated lactate on some analyzers
Increased anion gap
Increased osmolality gap
Mildly elevated creatinine
symptoms_not_in_common: Hyperchloremia is not a defining feature
Mild hyperglycemia is not a typical primary finding
No reported calcium oxalate crystals in urine
No reported hypocalcemia
No reported neurologic symptoms, cardiopulmonary symptoms, or renal failure

data.description: Methanol ingestion produces toxic formate metabolites, causing severe high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis and an increased osmolality gap, particularly early in poisoning.
symptoms_in_common: Acidemia
Low bicarbonate
Low PaCO2 from compensatory hyperventilation
Increased anion gap
Increased osmolality gap
Mildly elevated creatinine can occur in severe poisoning
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked lactate elevation is not usually the dominant laboratory abnormality
Hyperchloremia is not characteristic
Mild hyperglycemia is not typical
No reported visual disturbance or visual loss
No reported altered mental status, headache, abdominal pain, or coma

data.description: Propylene glycol exposure, often from intravenous medications such as lorazepam, diazepam, phenobarbital, or some formulations of nitroglycerin, can cause elevated osmolality gap, lactic acidosis, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, and kidney dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Acidemia
Low bicarbonate
Low PaCO2 consistent with respiratory compensation
Markedly elevated lactate
Increased anion gap
Increased osmolality gap
Mild creatinine elevation
symptoms_not_in_common: Hyperchloremia is not a classic primary feature
Mild hyperglycemia is not a typical defining finding
No reported exposure to propylene-glycol-containing intravenous medications
No reported prolonged intensive care medication infusion

data.description: A rare complication of metformin accumulation, usually in renal impairment, hypoperfusion, sepsis, or overdose, characterized by marked lactic acidosis and high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis.
symptoms_in_common: Acidemia
Low bicarbonate
Low PaCO2 due to respiratory compensation
Markedly elevated lactate
Increased anion gap
Mildly elevated creatinine
Mild hyperglycemia may occur in a patient with diabetes
symptoms_not_in_common: An increased osmolality gap is not typical
Hyperchloremia is not a defining feature
No reported metformin use
No reported diabetes history
No reported severe renal failure, shock, or sepsis

data.description: Diethylene glycol ingestion is a toxic alcohol exposure that can produce an elevated osmolality gap early, high-anion-gap metabolic acidosis, lactic acidosis, and progressive acute kidney injury.
symptoms_in_common: Acidemia
Low bicarbonate
Low PaCO2 consistent with respiratory compensation
Elevated lactate
Increased anion gap
Increased osmolality gap
Mildly elevated creatinine
symptoms_not_in_common: Hyperchloremia is not a characteristic finding
Mild hyperglycemia is not typical
Kidney injury is often more severe or progressive than the mild creatinine elevation described
No reported neurologic symptoms such as encephalopathy, neuropathy, or facial weakness
No reported exposure to contaminated medication, antifreeze, or industrial solvent

data.description: 6 weeks before current presentation and on current presentation: leukocytosis with neutrophilia (WBC 14,270 → 16,120/µL; neutrophils 10,130 → 12,280/µL), mild monocytosis, anemia (hemoglobin 10.9 → 10.1 g/dL; hematocrit 33.3% → 29.9%), platelet count normal (343,000 → 275,000/µL). ESR 19 mm/hr and CRP increased from 5.9 to 27.7 mg/L.

A rare chronic granulomatous inflammatory disorder caused by impaired macrophage bacterial killing, most often associated with Escherichia coli infection. It can form a large pelvic or abdominopelvic mass and mimic a gynecologic malignancy. Histology typically shows sheets of macrophages with Michaelis-Gutmann bodies.
symptoms_in_common: Large pelvic/abdominopelvic mass on MRI and CT
Progressive neutrophilic leukocytosis
Mild monocytosis
Anemia
Elevated CRP and inflammatory markers
Mass-like inflammatory lesion with histiocytic inflammatory appearance on pathology
symptoms_not_in_common: Normal platelet count is not a defining feature
ESR is only mildly elevated despite substantial inflammatory activity
No urinary-tract symptoms or documented recurrent urinary infection are provided

data.description: A destructive chronic inflammatory disease of the ovary and fallopian tube, often related to chronic pelvic infection. It produces a large solid-cystic pelvic mass with foamy macrophages, abscesses, fibrosis, and inflammatory cells, frequently resembling ovarian cancer radiologically.
symptoms_in_common: Large complex pelvic mass
Neutrophilic leukocytosis
Elevated CRP
Anemia of inflammation
Inflammatory mass-like pathology with macrophage-rich infiltrates
Possible abscess-like or necrotic areas within the mass
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever is reported
No pelvic pain, vaginal discharge, or adnexal tenderness is provided
No known history of pelvic inflammatory disease or intrauterine-device use is provided

data.description: A chronic invasive infection caused by Actinomyces species that can create infiltrative pelvic masses, abscesses, fibrosis, and adhesions. It commonly mimics advanced ovarian or pelvic malignancy and is particularly associated with long-term intrauterine-device use.
symptoms_in_common: Large infiltrative abdominopelvic mass
Neutrophilic leukocytosis
Increasing CRP
Anemia
Chronic inflammatory process with abscess-like histologic areas
Mass can involve adjacent pelvic and abdominal structures
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever is reported
No intrauterine-device history is provided
No vaginal discharge, pelvic pain, or bowel symptoms are described
No sulfur granules or filamentous bacteria are specifically reported

data.diagnosis: Epithelial ovarian carcinoma with inflammatory response
data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the ovary that may present as a large pelvic mass and can cause anemia and elevated inflammatory markers. Necrosis, tumor-associated inflammation, or superinfection can produce leukocytosis and high CRP.
symptoms_in_common: Large pelvic mass
Anemia
Elevated CRP
Possible abdominal/pelvic mass effect on imaging
Inflammatory laboratory abnormalities can occur in advanced or necrotic tumors
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked persistent neutrophilic leukocytosis is more suggestive of infection or inflammation than uncomplicated ovarian carcinoma

Apparent pallor
Peripheral blood smear appearance consistent with microcytic/hypochromic red cells

symptoms_in_common: Facial appearance potentially consistent with severe chronic anemia and marrow expansion
Apparent pallor
Red-cell abnormalities compatible with thalassemia
Hemoglobin H-type red-cell inclusions on supravital stain
symptoms_not_in_common: No hepatosplenomegaly is described

data.diagnosis: Beta-thalassemia major or severe beta-thalassemia intermedia
data.description: Inherited reduced or absent beta-globin production causing severe chronic microcytic anemia; untreated severe disease can produce marrow expansion and characteristic facial bone changes.

Apparent pallor
Red-cell morphology suggestive of a thalassemic microcytic anemia

data.description: A fibro-inflammatory disorder causing plaque-like soft tissue in the retroperitoneum, typically around the infrarenal aorta and iliac vessels, often entrapping and medially displacing the ureters.
symptoms_in_common: Coronal CT appearance of retroperitoneal soft-tissue thickening around the infrarenal aorta/common iliac region
Apparent involvement or medial displacement of the ureter
Possible ureteral obstruction/hydroureter suggested by the retroperitoneal process
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as flank pain, abdominal pain, weight loss, fever, or reduced urine output were provided

data.description: An immune-mediated form of retroperitoneal fibrosis associated with IgG4-related disease. It can produce a periaortic soft-tissue mantle and cause ureteral obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Retroperitoneal periaortic/iliac soft-tissue abnormality on CT
Possible ureteral encasement or medial displacement
Potential obstructive urinary tract involvement

data.description: Lymphoma may present with retroperitoneal nodal masses that surround major vessels and can compress the ureters, producing obstructive uropathy.

Possible ureteral compression and urinary tract obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No enlarged lymph nodes elsewhere were described
No B symptoms such as fever, night sweats, or weight loss were provided
The apparent plaque-like periaortic distribution is more characteristic of retroperitoneal fibrosis than bulky lymphoma

data.description: Metastatic cancer involving retroperitoneal lymph nodes or soft tissues can encase ureters and vessels, causing hydronephrosis or ureteral obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Retroperitoneal soft-tissue abnormality
Potential ureteral involvement or obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No known primary malignancy was provided
No multifocal masses, ascites, or widespread metastatic disease were described

data.description: Acute infection of lung parenchyma causing alveolar consolidation, which may involve one or more lobes and can produce near-complete opacification of a hemithorax when extensive.

Possible reduced right-lung aeration compared with the left lung

Involvement of medium-sized arteries

data.description: Troponin T was 0.03 on presentation and increased to 0.21 eight hours later. data.description: En la presentación: leucocitosis con neutrofilia (leucocitos 21.130/mm³, 80,2% PMNs), linfoopenia (7,4%), VS 34 mm/h, hiponatremia leve (Na 132 mmol/L) e hipocloremia (Cl 95 mmol/L). Un día antes, los glóbulos blancos eran 10.000/mm³; 9 semanas antes, hemoglobina 15,1 g/dL, hematócrito 45,6% y glóbulos blancos 10.000/mm³.
Una neumonía bacteriana atípica causada por especies de Legionella, a menudo asociada con hiponatremia, inflamación sistémica e infiltrados pulmonares de vidrio molido o nodulares en parches.

Tasa elevada de sedimentación de eritrocitos

Infiltraciones pulmonares bilaterales de vidrio molido/nodulos en TC

data.description: Anemia marcada con hematocrito/hemoglobina baja (HCT 33,2% en consulta externa, 26,7% al ingreso; Hb 10,7 a 8,6 g/dl) y microcitosis (MCV 79 fL), con leucopenia leve en consulta ambulatoria (leucocitos 3100/mm3) y linfopenia. El anticuerpo Helicobacter pylori fue positivo.

data.description: 3 months before presentation and on presentation, the patient had severe renal dysfunction (creatinine 8.33 to 16 mg/dl, BUN 44–45 mg/dl, eGFR 7 ml/min/1.73 m²) with anemia worsening from hematocrit 39.0% to 33.9% and hemoglobin 12.3 to 10.8 g/dl. No smoking history or known chronic obstructive pulmonary disease was provided

data.description: A pulmonary bulla is a large air-containing space caused by destruction and coalescence of alveoli; a giant bulla can occupy more than one-third of a hemithorax.
symptoms_in_common: Large, sharply defined air-containing intrathoracic space on CT
Possible compression of adjacent lung tissue
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported shortness of breath
No reported chest discomfort
No reported history of emphysema, smoking, or prior lung infection

data.description: Pneumothorax is air in the pleural space causing partial or complete collapse of the lung. Tension pneumothorax produces increased intrathoracic pressure and mediastinal shift and is a medical emergency.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly lucent air-filled right hemithorax on CT
Possible compression of intrathoracic structures
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute pleuritic chest pain was provided
No sudden dyspnea was provided
No hemodynamic instability, hypoxia, or tachycardia was provided
The image may show a giant intrapulmonary bulla rather than pleural air

data.description: A congenital airway abnormality causing progressive overinflation of one lung lobe, sometimes presenting later in childhood or adulthood and producing compression of adjacent lung.
symptoms_in_common: Marked unilateral hyperinflation/air-filled expansion of the right thorax
Potential compression of adjacent lung and mediastinal structures
symptoms_not_in_common: No age or childhood history was provided
No recurrent respiratory infections were provided
No chronic dyspnea or respiratory distress was provided

data.diagnosis: Primary bilateral macronodular adrenal hyperplasia (PBMAH) causing ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome
data.description: A disorder in which both adrenal glands develop nodular enlargement and autonomously produce cortisol, suppressing pituitary ACTH. It commonly presents later in adulthood and may cause mild or overt Cushing syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated cortisol after 1-mg dexamethasone suppression test
Elevated late-night salivary cortisol
Intermittently elevated 24-hour urinary free cortisol
Low to undetectable ACTH, consistent with ACTH-independent cortisol production
Bilateral adrenal abnormalities/enlargement on CT
Easy bruising
Diabetes/hyperglycemia with elevated fasting glucose and HbA1c
Older age at presentation
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria
Low-normal BMI rather than central obesity
No reported proximal muscle weakness, facial rounding, purple striae, or severe hypertension

data.description: Benign adrenal adenomas can autonomously secrete cortisol. Rarely, bilateral adenomas or an adenoma with contralateral adrenal nodularity can produce ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome.
symptoms_in_common: Left adrenal nodule measuring 1.7 cm
Contralateral adrenal enlargement
Failure of cortisol suppression after dexamethasone
Elevated late-night salivary cortisol
Elevated urinary free cortisol on several collections
Low or suppressed ACTH
Bruising
Hyperglycemia/diabetes
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria
Bilateral gland involvement is less typical than a single unilateral adenoma
Low BMI and absence of classic visible Cushingoid features

data.description: Cushing syndrome caused by autonomous adrenal cortisol secretion, most often from an adrenal adenoma or bilateral adrenal hyperplasia. Excess cortisol suppresses ACTH and can cause metabolic and skin manifestations.
symptoms_in_common: Cortisol remains markedly elevated after 1-mg dexamethasone suppression
Elevated late-night salivary cortisol
Elevated 24-hour urinary free cortisol
Low/undetectable ACTH
Adrenal nodular/enlargement findings on imaging
Easy bruising
Hyperglycemia and elevated HbA1c
Blood pressure above ideal range
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria
BMI is not elevated
No reported truncal obesity, moon facies, dorsocervical fat pad, striae, osteoporosis, or muscle weakness

data.description: A rare form of ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome caused by multiple small cortisol-producing adrenal nodules, often associated with Carney complex and more commonly diagnosed in children or young adults.
symptoms_in_common: ACTH-independent cortisol excess with low or suppressed ACTH
Abnormal dexamethasone suppression test
Elevated late-night salivary cortisol
Elevated urinary free cortisol
Bruising
Hyperglycemia
symptoms_not_in_common: Age 71 years, whereas PPNAD usually presents much earlier
Visible adrenal enlargement/nodule on CT, whereas PPNAD often has normal-sized or small adrenal glands
Hematuria
No reported features of Carney complex, such as lentigines, myxomas, or endocrine tumors

data.description: Laboratory evaluation showed normal hemoglobin, white-cell count, and platelets, with creatinine and glucose within range. Abnormal findings included low calcium, low total protein, marked hypoalbuminemia, elevated TSH with low free thyroxine, positive antinuclear antibodies at 1:40 with a speckled pattern, and urinalysis with 1+ blood and 3+ protein.
A renal syndrome caused by heavy urinary protein loss, leading to hypoalbuminemia, edema/anasarca, ascites, and sometimes secondary endocrine abnormalities from urinary loss of binding proteins.
symptoms_in_common: 3+ proteinuria
Marked hypoalbuminemia
Low total protein
Low calcium, which may reflect reduced albumin-bound calcium
Diffuse soft-tissue, mesenteric and retroperitoneal edema on CT
Possible ascites on pelvic CT
Normal creatinine can occur despite nephrotic-range proteinuria
Hypothyroidism can occur or worsen because thyroid hormone-binding proteins may be lost in urine
symptoms_not_in_common: 1+ blood on urinalysis is less typical in uncomplicated nephrotic syndrome
Positive antinuclear antibodies are not explained by nephrotic syndrome itself

data.diagnosis: Lupus nephritis due to systemic lupus erythematosus
data.description: Immune-complex kidney inflammation caused by systemic lupus erythematosus; it may produce proteinuria, hematuria, nephrotic syndrome, edema, and preserved creatinine early in the disease.
symptoms_in_common: Positive antinuclear antibodies with speckled pattern
Proteinuria
Microscopic hematuria suggested by 1+ blood on urinalysis
Marked hypoalbuminemia and low total protein due to urinary protein loss
Edema/anasarca with mesenteric, retroperitoneal and subcutaneous edema on CT
Possible ascites
Normal creatinine may be present in early or predominantly proteinuric lupus nephritis
symptoms_not_in_common: The ANA titer of 1:40 is low and is not by itself diagnostic of systemic lupus erythematosus
No reported rash, arthritis, oral ulcers, photosensitivity, cytopenias or other classic systemic lupus features
Hypothyroidism is not a typical direct manifestation of lupus nephritis

data.description: A podocyte disorder causing abrupt nephrotic syndrome, often with severe albumin loss and generalized edema while renal function remains normal or near normal.
symptoms_in_common: Heavy proteinuria indicated by 3+ urine protein
Marked hypoalbuminemia
Low total protein
Low calcium related to low serum albumin
Generalized edema, including subcutaneous and retroperitoneal edema on CT
Possible ascites
Normal creatinine
symptoms_not_in_common: Hematuria is less typical than in inflammatory glomerulonephritis
Positive ANA is not expected as a feature of primary minimal change disease
Elevated TSH with low free thyroxine is not a primary feature, although thyroid hormone-binding protein loss can contribute to abnormal thyroid tests

data.description: Excessive gastrointestinal loss of serum proteins causing profound hypoalbuminemia, edema, ascites, and low total protein; it may be associated with autoimmune disease such as lupus.
symptoms_in_common: Marked hypoalbuminemia
Low total protein
Low calcium due to hypoalbuminemia
Diffuse edema/anasarca on CT
Possible ascites
Positive ANA may support an autoimmune-associated cause
symptoms_not_in_common: 3+ proteinuria strongly suggests an important renal source of protein loss rather than isolated gastrointestinal protein loss
1+ blood on urinalysis is not typical
No reported diarrhea, abdominal pain, malabsorption or weight loss

data.description: Deficient thyroid hormone causes fatigue, weight gain, cold intolerance and edema; severe disease can contribute to serous effusions and generalized soft-tissue swelling.
symptoms_in_common: Elevated TSH
Low free thyroxine
Generalized soft-tissue edema on CT
Possible ascites or serous fluid accumulation
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked hypoalbuminemia and low total protein are not typical consequences of hypothyroidism alone
3+ proteinuria is not explained by uncomplicated hypothyroidism
Hematuria is not typical
Positive ANA is not a defining feature of hypothyroidism

diagnoses.name: Membranous nephropathy
diagnoses.title: Glomerular disease associated with thin basement membrane nephropathy

data.diagnosis: Gallbladder varices due to portal hypertension
data.description: Dilated collateral veins within or around the gallbladder wall caused by elevated portal venous pressure, often associated with portal vein obstruction or cavernous transformation.
symptoms_in_common: Ultrasound appearance of serpiginous anechoic structures in or adjacent to the gallbladder wall
MRI appearance of prominent vascular-appearing structures near the gallbladder and porta hepatis
Splenomegaly on MRI, supporting portal hypertension
Possible collateral vessels around the portal vein
symptoms_not_in_common: No abdominal pain, gastrointestinal bleeding, jaundice, or other clinical symptoms were provided

data.diagnosis: Chronic portal vein thrombosis with cavernous transformation
data.description: Long-standing portal vein obstruction can lead to formation of numerous periportal collateral veins (portal cavernoma), portal hypertension, splenomegaly, and gallbladder wall varices.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal vascular structures at the porta hepatis on MRI
Splenomegaly
Findings compatible with portal-systemic collateral formation
Gallbladder wall vascular channels consistent with collateral venous flow
symptoms_not_in_common: No known history of thrombosis, liver disease, variceal bleeding, ascites, or abdominal pain was provided

data.description: Gallbladder wall edema and/or varices occurring as a manifestation of portal hypertension, typically in patients with cirrhosis or extrahepatic portal venous obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Gallbladder wall abnormality on ultrasound
Possible intramural gallbladder venous collaterals
Splenomegaly, which can accompany portal hypertension
Periportal collateral vessels on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: No cirrhosis, ascites, jaundice, thrombocytopenia, or symptoms of chronic liver disease were described

data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis of medium-sized arteries that can cause multiple visceral arterial microaneurysms, stenoses, thrombosis, and renal infarction while usually sparing glomerular capillaries.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral renal cortical wedge-shaped perfusion defects compatible with renal infarcts
Multiple small renal arterial aneurysms or irregularities on angiography
Multifocal visceral arterial abnormalities involving renal and mesenteric-region vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: No constitutional symptoms, skin lesions, neuropathy, abdominal pain, hypertension, or laboratory findings are provided

data.description: A noninflammatory arteriopathy causing degeneration of the arterial media, with dissections, aneurysms, stenoses, and infarction, most often affecting abdominal visceral arteries.
symptoms_in_common: Multifocal abdominal visceral arterial aneurysmal and irregular vascular changes
Renal ischemic defects/infarcts
Possible involvement of more than one vascular territory
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute severe abdominal or flank pain is reported
No evidence of arterial rupture or retroperitoneal bleeding is provided
No hemodynamic instability is described

data.description: A nonatherosclerotic, noninflammatory disorder of medium-sized arteries, commonly renal and carotid arteries, producing alternating stenosis and dilatation (a string-of-beads appearance), aneurysms, dissections, or renal infarcts.
symptoms_in_common: Renal arterial irregularity with multifocal stenotic and aneurysmal-appearing changes
Renal perfusion defects that may occur after arterial dissection or thromboembolism
Bilateral renal vascular involvement is possible
symptoms_not_in_common: No hypertension is reported
No carotid or vertebral artery symptoms are described
Extensive visceral microaneurysms are less typical than in polyarteritis nodosa

data.diagnosis: Systemic vasculitis with renal medium-vessel involvement, such as ANCA-associated vasculitis
data.description: Systemic inflammatory vasculitides can cause renal vascular injury and ischemia, although small-vessel glomerulonephritis is generally more characteristic of ANCA-associated disease than multiple medium-vessel aneurysms.
symptoms_in_common: Renal abnormalities compatible with vascular injury or ischemia
Potential multifocal vascular involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Multiple medium-sized arterial microaneurysms are not typical of most ANCA-associated vasculitides
No hematuria, proteinuria, pulmonary symptoms, sinus disease, purpura, or inflammatory laboratory findings are provided

data.description: Progressive anemia over 16 months, with hemoglobin declining from 12.9 to 8.8 g/dl and hematocrit from 40.4% to 27.9%. Persistent inflammation with markedly elevated ESR and CRP. Chronic kidney dysfunction with creatinine rising from 4.61 to 7.03 mg/dl before admission and 8.09 mg/dl on admission, with elevated BUN. Leukocytosis was present intermittently, and there were episodes of eosinophilia and neutrophilia. Iron studies showed low iron and low iron-binding capacity with very high ferritin. Parathyroid hormone was elevated. Troponin T and NT-proBNP were elevated on admission. Interferon-gamma release assay for Mycobacterium tuberculosis was positive; HIV testing was nonreactive.

data.diagnosis: Tuberculous aortitis with infected abdominal aortic aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm
data.description: Rare extrapulmonary tuberculosis involving the aortic wall, causing inflammatory destruction, pseudoaneurysm or aneurysm formation, and sometimes fistulization into adjacent bowel or retroperitoneal structures.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated ESR and CRP
Progressive anemia
Intermittent leukocytosis
Positive interferon-gamma release assay for Mycobacterium tuberculosis
Pulmonary imaging abnormality compatible with possible tuberculosis
Abdominal aortic aneurysmal/pseudoaneurysmal inflammatory imaging findings
Periaortic and retroperitoneal inflammatory changes
Possible bowel involvement adjacent to the aneurysm
Chronic constitutional inflammatory pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe chronic kidney dysfunction is not a typical direct manifestation of isolated tuberculous aortitis
Elevated parathyroid hormone is more consistent with advanced chronic kidney disease
Elevated troponin T and NT-proBNP are not typical primary findings of tuberculous aortitis

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with pulmonary, gastrointestinal, and vascular involvement
data.description: Disseminated tuberculosis is infection affecting multiple organs outside the lungs, potentially including bowel, lymph nodes, kidneys, vascular structures, and the aorta. Gastrointestinal tuberculosis often involves the ileocecal region and may produce ulceration.
symptoms_in_common: Positive interferon-gamma release assay for tuberculosis
Persistent high inflammatory markers
Anemia of chronic inflammation
Very high ferritin with low iron and low iron-binding capacity
Intermittent leukocytosis
Eosinophilia and neutrophilia can occur during inflammatory or infectious complications
Pulmonary lesion on CT
Ileocecal or right-sided bowel ulcerative/inflammatory imaging and endoscopic findings
Aortic inflammatory aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm that could represent vascular tuberculosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Advanced renal failure is possible with renal tuberculosis but is not established by the provided findings
Secondary hyperparathyroidism is not a typical direct feature of tuberculosis
Cardiac biomarker elevation is not a usual defining feature of disseminated tuberculosis

data.diagnosis: Infected abdominal aortic aneurysm (mycotic aneurysm), possibly due to Mycobacterium tuberculosis
data.description: A mycotic aneurysm is an infected arterial aneurysm caused by microbial invasion of the vessel wall. It commonly causes rapid aneurysm expansion, periaortic inflammation, systemic inflammatory markers, anemia, and risk of rupture or fistula formation.
symptoms_in_common: Aneurysmal abdominal aortic imaging abnormality
Periaortic inflammatory changes
Markedly elevated ESR and CRP
Intermittent leukocytosis and neutrophilia
Progressive anemia
Possible communication or inflammatory involvement of adjacent bowel
Positive tuberculosis immune assay, supporting tuberculosis as one possible infectious cause
symptoms_not_in_common: Eosinophilia is not a typical feature of bacterial mycotic aneurysm
Chronic severe kidney failure is not usually caused by the aneurysm itself
Elevated parathyroid hormone is not characteristic
Pulmonary abnormalities are not required for a mycotic aneurysm

data.diagnosis: Aortoenteric fistula secondary to inflammatory or infected abdominal aortic aneurysm
data.description: An aortoenteric fistula is an abnormal communication between the aorta and gastrointestinal tract, usually associated with an aortic aneurysm, graft infection, or severe adjacent inflammation. It can cause occult or overt gastrointestinal bleeding, anemia, infection, and bowel ulceration.
symptoms_in_common: Progressive anemia that could reflect chronic occult gastrointestinal blood loss
Abdominal aortic aneurysm/pseudoaneurysm
Bowel abnormality adjacent to the aortic lesion
Endoscopic appearance of an ulcerated bowel lesion
High inflammatory markers
Intermittent leukocytosis
Possible infected aneurysm as an underlying cause
symptoms_not_in_common: No overt gastrointestinal hemorrhage, hematemesis, melena, or hematochezia is reported
Positive tuberculosis testing is not specific for aortoenteric fistula
Chronic kidney dysfunction and secondary hyperparathyroidism are not typical direct manifestations

data.diagnosis: Focal hepatic brucellosis (brucellar hepatic abscess/brucelloma) with erythema nodosum
data.description: A localized hepatic manifestation of Brucella infection, often occurring in Mediterranean regions such as Spain. It can produce a granulomatous liver mass or abscess and may be accompanied by immune-mediated skin findings including erythema nodosum.
symptoms_in_common: Large focal inflammatory lesion in the liver on CT
Erythematous tender-appearing nodules on the legs consistent with erythema nodosum
Granulomatous inflammatory changes on histology
Residence in Spain, a region where brucellosis occurs
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, sweats, fatigue, arthralgia, animal exposure, or unpasteurized dairy exposure is provided

data.description: Tuberculosis can cause granulomatous inflammation and focal hepatic lesions or abscess-like masses. Erythema nodosum can occur as a hypersensitivity reaction to tuberculosis.
symptoms_in_common: Focal hepatic mass or abscess-like lesion
Granulomatous histologic appearance
Erythema nodosum-like lesions on the lower extremities
symptoms_not_in_common: No respiratory symptoms, prolonged fever, weight loss, night sweats, or known tuberculosis exposure is provided
A solitary large hepatic lesion is less typical than disseminated or multifocal hepatic involvement

data.description: Systemic Bartonella henselae infection can cause hepatic or splenic granulomatous lesions in immunocompetent patients and may be associated with erythema nodosum or other inflammatory skin eruptions.
symptoms_in_common: Hepatic inflammatory lesion on CT
Possible granulomatous inflammation on histology
Erythema nodosum-like rash on the legs
symptoms_not_in_common: No cat exposure, scratch, regional lymphadenopathy, fever, or splenic lesions is provided
A single large hepatic lesion is less typical than multiple small hepatic and splenic lesions

data.description: An abnormal direct connection between meningeal arteries and dural venous sinuses or cortical veins, which can cause venous congestion and prominent tortuous intracranial vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent serpiginous intracranial vascular structures on angiographic imaging
Possible diffuse venous engorgement/cortical venous prominence
Possible abnormal dural enhancement
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as pulsatile tinnitus, headache, seizures, focal neurologic deficit, or intracranial hemorrhage were provided

data.diagnosis: Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis with collateral venous circulation
data.description: Thrombosis of a dural venous sinus can obstruct cerebral venous drainage and lead to enlarged collateral cortical and extracranial veins, venous congestion, and sometimes hemorrhagic infarction.
symptoms_in_common: Prominent cortical and dural venous channels on imaging
Possible abnormal venous drainage pattern
Possible diffuse venous congestion
symptoms_not_in_common: No headache was reported
No papilledema or visual symptoms were reported
No seizures, focal weakness, altered consciousness, or hemorrhagic infarction symptoms were provided

data.description: A congenital vascular malformation consisting of abnormal high-flow connections between arteries and veins, often producing a tangle of enlarged vessels and early venous drainage.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal prominent intracranial vessels on angiographic imaging
Possible enlarged draining veins
symptoms_not_in_common: No focal nidus of abnormal vessels is clearly described
No seizures were reported
No intracranial hemorrhage was reported
No headache, focal neurologic deficit, or bruit was provided

data.description: A benign vascular liver tumor, often incidentally detected. On contrast CT it commonly shows peripheral nodular enhancement with progressive centripetal fill-in; large lesions may be heterogeneous.
symptoms_in_common: Large well-circumscribed hepatic mass on contrast-enhanced CT
Peripheral nodular enhancement of the lesion
Progressive enhancement/fill-in pattern on sequential contrast images
Additional small hyperenhancing hepatic foci may represent multiple hemangiomas
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms, laboratory abnormalities, or relevant medical history were provided

data.description: A benign hyperplastic liver lesion composed of normal hepatocytes and abnormal vessels. It is usually asymptomatic and may show strong arterial enhancement with a central scar and delayed scar enhancement.
symptoms_in_common: Solitary dominant liver mass
Relatively well-defined lesion
Possible central stellate scar-like area
Hypervascular appearance on contrast-enhanced CT
symptoms_not_in_common: Peripheral discontinuous nodular enhancement with progressive fill-in is more characteristic of hemangioma than focal nodular hyperplasia
No clinical symptoms, laboratory abnormalities, or relevant medical history were provided

data.description: A benign hepatocellular tumor that may occur in people with hormonal exposure, obesity, metabolic disease, or anabolic steroid use. It can be hypervascular and may hemorrhage or undergo malignant transformation in selected subtypes.
symptoms_in_common: Large hepatic mass
Possible arterial-phase hyperenhancement
May be incidentally discovered without symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: Progressive peripheral nodular enhancement is not the typical enhancement pattern for hepatocellular adenoma
No hemorrhage, fat within the lesion, hormonal exposure, metabolic risk factors, or laboratory findings were provided

data.diagnosis: Hepatic metastases from a hypervascular primary tumor
data.description: Metastatic liver disease occurs when a malignancy from another organ spreads to the liver. Hypervascular metastases may arise from neuroendocrine tumors, renal cell carcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, melanoma, or some other primary cancers.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple hepatic lesions may be present
Some lesions may enhance prominently after contrast administration
symptoms_not_in_common: A dominant lesion with peripheral nodular progressive fill-in is less typical of metastasis and favors hemangioma
No known primary malignancy, weight loss, systemic symptoms, or lymphadenopathy was provided

data.description: A disorder caused by excess growth hormone, usually from a pituitary adenoma, producing progressive enlargement of the hands, feet, facial bones, and soft tissues.
symptoms_in_common: Marked enlargement of the feet and toes
Broad, enlarged hand with thickened soft tissues
Bulbous enlargement of digits
Thickened, swollen-appearing skin
symptoms_not_in_common: Focal violaceous or hemorrhagic-looking lesions on several toes
Apparent skin erosions or ulcerated areas on the toes
Markedly asymmetric nodular swelling of individual toes

data.description: A rare genetic condition characterized by clubbing of the fingers and toes, thickened skin, enlargement of distal extremities, and periosteal new bone formation.
symptoms_in_common: Enlarged bulbous distal fingers and toes
Possible digital clubbing
Thickened skin of the hands and feet
Large hands and feet with soft-tissue swelling
symptoms_not_in_common: Toe lesions that appear bruised, eroded, or ulcerated
Prominent localized nodules on the toes
No visible evidence of the typical facial pachydermia or excessive sweating

data.description: Persistent failure of lymphatic drainage causing progressive swelling, skin thickening, fibrosis, recurrent inflammation, and deformity of an affected limb or foot.
symptoms_in_common: Massive swelling of the forefoot and toes
Thickened and stretched skin
Distorted enlarged digits
Possible chronic skin breakdown or superficial erosions
symptoms_not_in_common: Enlargement of the hand, which would be unusual unless there is generalized or multifocal lymphedema
Bulbous clubbing-like appearance of the fingers
No obvious verrucous, hyperkeratotic, or papillomatous skin changes typical of advanced elephantiasis

data.description: A disorder of monosodium urate crystal deposition that can cause recurrent inflammatory arthritis, destructive joint deformity, and firm tophi around joints, toes, fingers, and nail areas.
symptoms_in_common: Nodular enlargement around multiple toe joints
Possible inflammatory redness and violaceous discoloration
Deformed toes and possible joint destruction
Potential skin ulceration over prominent nodules
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse massive soft-tissue enlargement of the entire foot
Generalized thickened appearance of the hand
No clearly visible chalky white tophaceous material

data.description: An inflammatory arthritis associated with psoriasis that may cause swollen 'sausage' digits, joint damage, nail abnormalities, and deformity of hands and feet.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse enlargement of individual toes resembling dactylitis
Swollen fingers and toes
Possible nail dystrophy or thickened nails
Possible inflammatory red-purple discoloration of digits
symptoms_not_in_common: Extreme massive enlargement of the whole foot is atypical
No visible psoriatic plaques or characteristic scale
No obvious typical nail pitting, onycholysis, or widespread psoriasis

data.description: A saddleback ST-segment elevation pattern in the right precordial leads, usually V1-V2, which can suggest Brugada syndrome but is not diagnostic without a type 1 pattern and appropriate clinical context.
symptoms_in_common: Saddleback-shaped ST-segment elevation in V2
Prominent r' or terminal R-wave appearance in V2
Right-precordial ECG abnormality involving V1-V3
symptoms_not_in_common: No syncope, nocturnal agonal breathing, palpitations, ventricular arrhythmia, cardiac arrest, or family history of sudden cardiac death was provided

data.description: An inherited cardiac sodium-channel disorder that predisposes to polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, ventricular fibrillation, and sudden cardiac death. Diagnosis generally requires a spontaneous or provoked type 1 Brugada ECG pattern plus supportive clinical evaluation.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal ST-segment morphology in the right precordial leads
Possible Brugada-like saddleback configuration in V2
symptoms_not_in_common: The ECG shown appears more consistent with a type 2 saddleback pattern than the diagnostic type 1 coved pattern
No history of unexplained syncope
No documented ventricular tachycardia or ventricular fibrillation
No cardiac arrest
No family history of sudden unexplained death was provided

data.description: A conduction delay through the right bundle branch that may produce an rSr' or rsR' pattern in V1-V2 with a narrow or mildly prolonged QRS duration. It is often benign but can resemble Brugada-pattern ECG changes.
symptoms_in_common: r' or terminal positive deflection in V2
Right-precordial conduction-pattern abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent saddleback ST-segment elevation is less typical for uncomplicated incomplete right bundle branch block
No symptoms such as palpitations, syncope, or dyspnea were provided

data.description: A usually benign ECG variant characterized by J-point elevation and mild concave ST-segment elevation, commonly seen in healthy individuals and sometimes extending into precordial leads.
symptoms_in_common: Mild ST-segment elevation in precordial leads
J-point or terminal QRS-ST transition elevation
symptoms_not_in_common: The focal saddleback morphology in V2 is more suggestive of a Brugada-like pattern than typical diffuse early repolarization
No clinical symptoms were provided

data.diagnosis: HIV/AIDS with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia and cerebral toxoplasmosis
data.description: Advanced HIV infection can cause simultaneous opportunistic infections, including diffuse Pneumocystis pneumonia in the lungs and multifocal toxoplasmosis lesions in the brain.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral diffuse ground-glass pulmonary opacities on CT, compatible with Pneumocystis pneumonia
Multiple bilateral cerebellar/brain lesions on MRI, compatible with cerebral toxoplasmosis
Multifocal central nervous system involvement
Pattern suggestive of opportunistic infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No respiratory symptoms such as cough, dyspnea, fever, or hypoxemia are provided
No neurologic symptoms such as headache, seizures, confusion, focal weakness, or ataxia are provided
No HIV status, CD4 count, or immunosuppression history is provided

data.diagnosis: Disseminated tuberculosis with pulmonary and central nervous system involvement
data.description: Tuberculosis can disseminate from the lungs to the brain, producing pulmonary nodules or infiltrates and intracranial tuberculomas or meningitis.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral pulmonary abnormalities on CT
Multifocal brain lesions, including posterior fossa/cerebellar involvement
Potential hematogenous dissemination affecting lung and brain
Residence in Spain, where tuberculosis remains a relevant diagnostic consideration
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, night sweats, weight loss, chronic cough, or hemoptysis are reported
No meningitic symptoms such as neck stiffness or persistent headache are reported
The described diffuse ground-glass lung pattern is less classic than cavitary, miliary, or upper-lobe predominant tuberculosis

data.diagnosis: Disseminated cryptococcosis with pulmonary cryptococcosis and cryptococcal CNS disease
data.description: Cryptococcus is an opportunistic fungal infection that may involve the lungs and central nervous system, particularly in people with advanced immunosuppression.
symptoms_in_common: Pulmonary infiltrative/nodular abnormalities on CT
Multifocal brain MRI abnormalities
Possible combined lung and CNS infection
Imaging pattern that could occur in an immunocompromised patient
symptoms_not_in_common: No headache, fever, nausea, confusion, visual symptoms, or meningismus are provided
No evidence of elevated intracranial pressure is described
No known immunosuppression or HIV infection is provided

data.diagnosis: Pulmonary nocardiosis with disseminated nocardial brain abscesses
data.description: Nocardia can cause lung infection followed by hematogenous spread to the brain, where it may produce multiple abscesses; it is more common in immunocompromised patients.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal bilateral pulmonary CT findings
Multiple intracranial lesions on MRI
Potential lung-to-brain dissemination
Posterior fossa/cerebellar lesions can occur with nocardial brain abscesses
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, productive cough, chest pain, or shortness of breath are reported
No focal neurologic deficits, seizures, or headache are reported
The lung CT appearance is not described as cavitary consolidation, which is a common nocardial pattern

data.description: Sarcoidosis is a systemic granulomatous inflammatory disease that commonly affects the lungs and can less commonly affect the central nervous system.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral pulmonary abnormalities
Central nervous system lesions on MRI
Potential multisystem inflammatory disease involving lungs and brain
symptoms_not_in_common: No hilar or mediastinal lymphadenopathy is described
No cranial neuropathies, facial weakness, visual symptoms, or endocrine abnormalities are reported
Multiple cerebellar mass-like lesions are less typical than meningeal, cranial nerve, or hypothalamic-pituitary involvement

data.diagnosis: Deep infiltrating intestinal endometriosis with ureteral involvement
data.description: Endometriosis is the presence of endometrial-type glands and stroma outside the uterus. Deep infiltrating disease can involve the bowel wall and ureter, producing inflammatory masses, bowel narrowing, and urinary obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Endoscopic inflammatory, ulcerated, stenosing bowel lesion
