data.diagnosis: Left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), possibly related to hypertension
data.description: Thickening of the left ventricular heart muscle, often caused by longstanding high blood pressure or other conditions that increase cardiac workload. The ECG shows high QRS voltage compatible with LVH.
symptoms_in_common: ECG with increased precordial QRS voltage
Deep S waves in V1-V3 with tall R waves in V4-V6
Voltage sum reported as R(V5) plus S(V1) = 3.45 mV, meeting a common ECG voltage criterion for LVH

data.description: Structural and functional heart changes caused by chronic arterial hypertension, commonly including left ventricular hypertrophy and later diastolic dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: ECG pattern suggestive of left ventricular hypertrophy
Sinus rhythm with high-voltage QRS complexes
symptoms_not_in_common: No blood pressure measurements or history of hypertension provided
No reported chest pain, shortness of breath, edema, headache, or exertional symptoms

data.description: A usually inherited condition characterized by abnormal thickening of the heart muscle, often involving the interventricular septum. It can produce high ECG voltage and repolarization abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: High-voltage QRS complexes compatible with increased ventricular muscle mass
Possible mild ST-T wave changes in precordial leads
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported syncope, exertional chest pain, palpitations, shortness of breath, or family history of sudden cardiac death
No characteristic marked T-wave inversion or pathological Q waves described

data.diagnosis: Normal sinus rhythm with benign high QRS voltage
data.description: Some individuals, particularly younger or thin patients and athletes, can have high-voltage ECG complexes without structural heart disease. The tracing appears to show a regular sinus rhythm.
symptoms_in_common: Regular sinus rhythm at approximately 68 beats per minute
Normal reported PR interval of 172 ms
High QRS voltage without clearly documented clinical symptoms
symptoms_not_in_common: QRS duration of 120 ms is borderline prolonged and may warrant clinical correlation
Voltage criteria for LVH are present, so structural heart disease should be excluded when clinically appropriate

data.description: A small air-filled outpouching arising from the tracheal wall, most often located at the right posterolateral upper thoracic trachea. It is commonly an incidental congenital or acquired finding.
symptoms_in_common: No clinical symptoms were provided
Small right paratracheal air-containing outpouching visible on CT
Chest radiograph without acute pulmonary abnormality
symptoms_not_in_common: No patient symptoms were reported

data.description: A congenital anatomic variant in which an accessory bronchus arises directly from the trachea, usually on the right side and often supplying the right upper lobe. It may be asymptomatic or predispose to recurrent infection.
symptoms_in_common: No clinical symptoms were provided
Possible small airway-like structure adjacent to the right side of the trachea on CT
No acute infiltrate on chest radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: No recurrent pneumonia reported
No chronic cough reported
No wheezing or respiratory distress reported

data.description: Free air within the mediastinum, typically caused by alveolar rupture, trauma, vomiting, severe coughing, or esophageal injury. CT usually shows linear or loculated mediastinal air around the trachea and vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Small paratracheal air focus on CT
symptoms_not_in_common: No chest pain reported
No shortness of breath reported
No neck swelling or subcutaneous emphysema reported
No acute radiographic mediastinal air pattern described

data.description: An expanding red skin lesion caused by Borrelia infection after an Ixodes tick bite. It may form an annular or target-like rash and can occur without fever or other systemic symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Large expanding-looking red annular lesion
Central relative clearing/paler area
Target-like or bull's-eye appearance
Location in Spain, where Lyme disease can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Purplish or bruise-like discoloration in the center is less typical
No tick bite, fever, fatigue, headache, or joint symptoms were reported

data.description: A superficial fungal skin infection that produces a round or ring-shaped red rash, often with a more active outer border and central clearing.
symptoms_in_common: Ring-shaped red lesion
More prominent red border
Central clearing or lighter central skin
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears unusually large and smooth rather than scaly
No itchiness was reported

Central purple bruising is not typical

data.description: Skin inflammation caused by contact with an allergen or irritant, such as adhesive, clothing, topical products, plants, or chemicals. It can cause localized redness with sharply defined borders.

Relatively well-demarcated border
Possible shape suggestive of contact with an object, adhesive, or external substance
symptoms_not_in_common: Annular target-like configuration is less typical
Central clearing is less typical
No itching, burning, blistering, or known exposure was reported

data.description: A localized medication-related skin reaction that often appears as a sharply defined red, dusky, or violaceous patch and may recur in the same location after taking a medication.
symptoms_in_common: Sharply outlined red lesion
Dusky purple or bruise-like central discoloration
Single localized patch
symptoms_not_in_common: Ring-shaped border with central clearing is less characteristic
No recent medication exposure or recurrent episodes were reported
No burning, itching, or blistering was reported

data.description: A localized inflammatory reaction after a bite from a tick, mosquito, spider, or other arthropod. Reactions may cause redness, swelling, itching, and occasionally a target-like pattern.
symptoms_in_common: Localized erythematous lesion
Possible target-like appearance
Central discoloration that could reflect bite-related inflammation or minor bruising
symptoms_not_in_common: No bite, puncture mark, itching, pain, or swelling was reported
The large annular pattern is more suggestive of erythema migrans than a simple bite reaction

data.description: A nontraumatic tear or intramural hematoma within a coronary artery wall that narrows the true lumen and can cause acute coronary syndrome, often without major atherosclerotic plaque.
symptoms_in_common: Electrocardiographic ischemic ST-segment and T-wave changes
Coronary angiographic appearance of a long smooth narrowing compatible with dissection or intramural hematoma
Intravascular ultrasound appearance suggestive of vessel-wall hematoma or false-lumen compression
symptoms_not_in_common: No chest pain, dyspnea, palpitations, syncope, or other clinical symptoms were provided

data.description: Myocardial ischemia caused by reduced coronary blood flow without persistent ST-segment elevation; it may result from plaque disruption, coronary dissection, spasm, or other coronary obstruction.
symptoms_in_common: Widespread ischemic ECG abnormalities, including ST-segment depression and repolarization changes
Coronary abnormality demonstrated on angiography
Evidence of clinically important coronary luminal compromise on intravascular imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute chest discomfort or pressure was reported
No cardiac troponin result was provided
No nausea, sweating, dyspnea, or radiation of pain was reported

data.description: Transient constriction of an epicardial coronary artery that produces myocardial ischemia, often with reversible angiographic narrowing and transient ECG changes.
symptoms_in_common: Ischemic ECG changes
Angiographically apparent coronary narrowing that could potentially represent dynamic vasoconstriction
symptoms_not_in_common: No episodic rest chest pain was reported
No temporal relationship to rest, nighttime, smoking, or vasospasm-provoking exposures was provided
Intravascular ultrasound findings suggesting intramural hematoma would be less typical than for SCAD

data.diagnosis: Obstructive coronary artery disease due to atherosclerotic plaque
data.description: Coronary narrowing caused by cholesterol-rich plaque accumulation, which can impair myocardial blood flow or lead to acute plaque rupture and myocardial infarction.
symptoms_in_common: ECG findings compatible with myocardial ischemia
Coronary luminal narrowing seen during angiography
Coronary wall abnormality on intravascular imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent long smooth narrowing and possible intramural hematoma pattern are less typical of focal atherosclerotic plaque
No cardiovascular risk factors, prior coronary disease, or lipid history were provided
No exertional angina history was reported

data.description: A genetic TP63-associated disorder characterized by split-hand/split-foot malformations, ectodermal abnormalities such as missing teeth, and sometimes cleft lip or palate.
symptoms_in_common: Bilateral congenital hand malformations with absent or underdeveloped digits
Bilateral foot malformations with absent or fused toes
Marked oligodontia or hypodontia on panoramic dental radiograph
symptoms_not_in_common: Cleft lip or cleft palate is not shown or reported

data.description: A congenital limb-malformation spectrum involving ectrodactyly or split-hand/split-foot deformities, sometimes associated with tibial or other long-bone defects.
symptoms_in_common: Congenital bilateral hand digital reduction/deformity
Congenital bilateral foot toe reduction/deformity
Appearance compatible with split-hand/split-foot spectrum
symptoms_not_in_common: Severe tooth agenesis is not a usual feature of isolated SHFLD
Long-bone deficiency is not shown or reported

data.description: A TP63-related ectodermal dysplasia syndrome that may include hypodontia, clefting, skin and hair abnormalities, and occasionally limb malformations.
symptoms_in_common: Multiple missing teeth or delayed/abnormal tooth development
Congenital hand and foot abnormalities can occur in TP63-related disorders
symptoms_not_in_common: Ankyloblepharon (fused eyelids) is not reported
Scalp erosions, sparse hair, and skin abnormalities are not reported
The pronounced split-hand/split-foot pattern is more characteristic of EEC syndrome than AEC syndrome
Cleft lip or palate is not shown or reported

data.description: A TP63-associated ectodermal dysplasia characterized by hypodontia or oligodontia, abnormal hair and nails, cleft lip or palate in some individuals, and variable limb abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Extensive congenital absence of teeth
Possible congenital digital abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Sparse hair, nail dystrophy, and sweating abnormalities are not reported
Cleft lip or palate is not shown or reported
Severe split-hand/split-foot-type limb malformations are less typical than in EEC syndrome

data.diagnosis: Frequent premature atrial contractions with nonsustained atrial tachycardia
data.description: Premature atrial contractions are early beats arising from the atria. When recurrent consecutive atrial beats occur, they can produce short runs of atrial tachycardia; a high burden may trigger or coexist with atrial fibrillation.

data.diagnosis: Gastric extranodal marginal zone lymphoma of mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue (gastric MALT lymphoma)
data.description: An indolent B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma arising in the stomach, commonly associated with Helicobacter pylori infection. It can cause erosions, ulcers, enlarged gastric folds, and dense lymphoid infiltration with lymphoepithelial lesions on biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal gastric mucosa with erythema, erosive/ulcerated areas, and irregular thickened folds on endoscopy
Dense lymphoid infiltrate in gastric biopsy tissue
Histologic appearance compatible with lymphoepithelial lesions involving gastric glands
Immunohistochemical staining pattern suggesting a B-cell lymphoid proliferation

data.description: A malignant epithelial tumor of the stomach. It may appear endoscopically as an ulcerated, irregular, infiltrative, or depressed lesion and is confirmed by biopsy showing malignant atypical glands invading the gastric wall.
symptoms_in_common: Irregular gastric lesion with abnormal mucosal architecture on endoscopy
Ulcerated or infiltrative-appearing gastric mucosal lesion
Biopsy images showing atypical glandular structures within desmoplastic/inflammatory stroma, compatible with invasive adenocarcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent diffuse lymphoid infiltrate and lymphoepithelial-type lesions are more characteristic of gastric MALT lymphoma than adenocarcinoma

data.description: Chronic gastric inflammation caused by Helicobacter pylori infection. It can produce erythema, erosions, ulceration, lymphoid follicle formation, and may predispose to both peptic ulcer disease and gastric MALT lymphoma.
symptoms_in_common: Gastric mucosal erythema and erosive/ulcerated changes on endoscopy
Dense chronic inflammatory and lymphoid infiltrates in gastric tissue
Gastric lymphoid tissue proliferation, which is often associated with H. pylori infection
symptoms_not_in_common: The apparent monoclonal or extensive lymphomatous B-cell proliferation would not be typical of uncomplicated gastritis
Invasive atypical glands would suggest adenocarcinoma rather than gastritis alone

data.diagnosis: Late-presenting left congenital diaphragmatic hernia (Bochdalek hernia) with intrathoracic stomach
data.description: A congenital posterolateral diaphragmatic defect permits abdominal organs, particularly the stomach, to herniate into the thorax. It can present later in childhood or adulthood and mimic a pleural air-fluid collection.
symptoms_in_common: Large left-sided intrathoracic air-fluid level
Apparent compression/collapse of the left lung
Nasogastric tube projecting and coiling within the left hemithorax, consistent with an intrathoracic stomach
Poor visualization or displacement of the left hemidiaphragm
symptoms_not_in_common: No gastrointestinal symptoms such as vomiting, abdominal pain, or feeding intolerance were reported
No respiratory symptoms such as dyspnea, chest pain, or cyanosis were reported

data.diagnosis: Paraesophageal hiatal hernia with intrathoracic stomach
data.description: A hiatal hernia occurs when the stomach herniates through the esophageal hiatus into the chest. A large paraesophageal hernia may create a retrocardiac or left thoracic air-fluid level and can predispose to gastric volvulus.
symptoms_in_common: Large air-fluid level in the left lower thorax
Enteric tube seen within a structure in the left thorax, compatible with intrathoracic stomach
Compression of adjacent left lung
symptoms_not_in_common: The radiographic extent may be more lateral and extensive than is typical for a simple hiatal hernia
No reflux, dysphagia, postprandial chest discomfort, vomiting, or epigastric pain was reported

data.diagnosis: Gastric volvulus associated with diaphragmatic hernia
data.description: Gastric volvulus is abnormal twisting of the stomach, often associated with a diaphragmatic defect or paraesophageal hernia. It may result in a distended intrathoracic stomach with an air-fluid level and can become an emergency if strangulation occurs.
symptoms_in_common: Marked intrathoracic gastric-type air-fluid level
Possible abnormal configuration and distension of the intrathoracic stomach
Nasogastric tube coiling within the thoracic stomach
Left lung compression
symptoms_not_in_common: No acute severe epigastric or chest pain was reported
No retching or inability to vomit was reported
No difficulty passing a nasogastric tube was reported

data.description: Hydropneumothorax is the presence of both air and fluid in the pleural space; when infected it is called pyopneumothorax. It produces a pleural air-fluid level and can compress the lung.
symptoms_in_common: Large left thoracic air-fluid level
Compression of the left lung
symptoms_not_in_common: The enteric tube coiling in the left hemithorax is not typical of pleural air and fluid and instead suggests an intrathoracic stomach
No fever, productive cough, pleuritic chest pain, trauma, or acute shortness of breath was reported
The appearance is less typical of a simple pleural collection when bowel or gastric herniation is considered

data.description: An IgG4-related fibroinflammatory disease of the pancreas characterized by pancreatic enlargement, dense lymphoplasmacytic inflammation, storiform fibrosis, and increased IgG4-positive plasma cells.
symptoms_in_common: Diffuse or segmental pancreatic enlargement on cross-sectional imaging
Pancreatic mass-like inflammatory appearance that can mimic malignancy
Dense lymphoplasmacytic inflammatory infiltrate on biopsy
Prominent plasma-cell immunostaining, compatible with increased IgG4-positive plasma cells

data.description: A lymphoma arising predominantly in the pancreas, often producing a bulky pancreatic mass or diffuse pancreatic enlargement and sometimes resembling pancreatitis or pancreatic carcinoma on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Mass-like or enlarged pancreas on CT/MRI
Dense lymphoid cellular infiltrate in pancreatic biopsy material
Imaging appearance that may not show the classic ductal obstruction expected with pancreatic adenocarcinoma
symptoms_not_in_common: Plasma-cell-rich infiltrate with apparent IgG4-associated immunostaining is more characteristic of autoimmune pancreatitis than lymphoma
No described atypical lymphoid-cell morphology or definite monoclonal B-cell immunophenotype

data.description: The most common pancreatic malignancy, typically an infiltrating duct-forming carcinoma that causes a focal pancreatic mass, biliary obstruction, pancreatic duct dilatation, and metastatic disease.
symptoms_in_common: Focal or mass-like pancreatic abnormality on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Diffuse inflammatory pancreatic enlargement is less typical than a discrete infiltrative mass
Dense lymphoplasmacytic and plasma-cell-predominant biopsy findings are not typical of adenocarcinoma
No described malignant ductal glands, marked cytologic atypia, or desmoplastic invasive carcinoma
No reported pancreatic or bile-duct obstruction

data.description: Long-standing pancreatic inflammation causing fibrosis and loss of exocrine tissue; it may form an inflammatory pancreatic mass and can overlap radiologically with autoimmune pancreatitis.
symptoms_in_common: Pancreatic inflammatory enlargement
Inflammatory infiltrate and fibrosis on pancreatic tissue sampling
Mass-like inflammatory pancreatic changes can occur
symptoms_not_in_common: Marked lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate with apparent IgG4-positive plasma-cell staining is more suggestive of type 1 autoimmune pancreatitis
No reported pancreatic calcifications
No reported pancreatic duct irregularity, duct stones, or established pancreatic atrophy

data.description: Antimicrobial susceptibility and typing results for three bacterial strains (A8806, H041, F89): ceftriaxone resistant; penicillin G resistant/intermediate; ciprofloxacin resistant; azithromycin susceptible in A8806 but resistant in H041 and F89; spectinomycin susceptible. Multilocus sequence types: 7363, 7363, and 1901. Multiantigen sequence types: 4015, 4220, and 1407. Mosaic penicillin-binding protein 2 alterations reported: A311V/T483ST1, A311V/T316P/T483S, and A501P.

A sexually transmitted bacterial infection caused by Neisseria gonorrhoeae. The reported sequence types, mosaic penicillin-binding protein 2 mutations, and antimicrobial susceptibility profile are characteristic of gonococcal isolates.
symptoms_in_common: Detection of bacterial strains with Neisseria gonorrhoeae multilocus sequence types 7363 and 1901
Mosaic penicillin-binding protein 2 alterations associated with gonococcal beta-lactam resistance
Resistance or reduced susceptibility to penicillin G
Ciprofloxacin resistance
Ceftriaxone resistance

data.description: Gonorrhea caused by N. gonorrhoeae with resistance to ceftriaxone, an extended-spectrum cephalosporin commonly used as first-line therapy. This is a major public-health concern because it can limit standard treatment options.
symptoms_in_common: Ceftriaxone-resistant isolates A8806, H041, and F89
Mosaic penicillin-binding protein 2 mutations associated with cephalosporin resistance
Penicillin G resistance or intermediate susceptibility
Ciprofloxacin resistance
Spectinomycin susceptibility
symptoms_not_in_common: No genital, rectal, pharyngeal, urinary, or systemic clinical symptoms were provided

data.description: An infection with N. gonorrhoeae resistant to multiple antimicrobial classes, including cephalosporins, penicillins, and fluoroquinolones. Some isolates also show macrolide resistance.

Resistance or intermediate susceptibility to penicillin G
Resistance to ciprofloxacin
Azithromycin resistance in strains H041 and F89
Gonococcal molecular typing results consistent with recognized resistant lineages
Mosaic penicillin-binding protein 2 alterations
symptoms_not_in_common: Azithromycin susceptibility in strain A8806, because not all isolates are resistant to this agent

data.description: A severe form of bullous emphysema in which very large air-filled bullae replace or compress normal lung tissue, often causing marked unilateral hyperlucency and reduced functional lung volume.

Compression of adjacent residual lung tissue
Hyperinflation/emphysematous appearance of the lungs

No clinical symptoms such as progressive dyspnea, cough, smoking history, or chest pain were provided

Large emphysematous bulla in the left lung
Reduced visible vascular markings within the large air-filled area

Large left basilar air-filled bulla

data.diagnosis: Bronchiectasis with secondary localized emphysematous/bullous change
data.description: Bronchiectasis is permanent dilation and distortion of bronchi caused by chronic infection, inflammation, or impaired airway clearance; regional air trapping and destructive lung changes can coexist.

data.description: A highly aggressive mature B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphoma that commonly presents with a rapidly growing bulky abdominal or retroperitoneal mass and may involve kidneys, bowel, bone marrow, and other extranodal sites.

Potential renal involvement or infiltration
Lymphoid tumor infiltrating tissue structures

data.description: A necrotizing vasculitis affecting small- to medium-sized arteries in the skin, often producing livedo reticularis/racemosa, purpura, painful nodules, ulcers, or infarct-like lesions. Biopsy may show inflamed vessel walls with fibrinoid necrosis and luminal thrombosis.

Biopsy appearance of an inflamed vessel with fibrinous change and thrombotic occlusion

data.diagnosis: Antiphospholipid syndrome with cutaneous thrombotic vasculopathy

Thrombosed cutaneous vessel on histology

data.description: An immune-complex-mediated inflammation of small dermal vessels that commonly causes palpable purpura and may be triggered by infection, medications, autoimmune disease, or malignancy. Histology can show vessel-wall injury, fibrinoid necrosis, and inflammatory cell infiltration.

data.diagnosis: Classic homocystinuria due to cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS) deficiency
data.description: An inherited disorder of transsulfuration causing markedly elevated homocysteine and methionine. It commonly produces ectopia lentis, marfanoid skeletal features, osteoporosis, and increased thromboembolic risk.

Lens subluxation/ectopia lentis

No aortic root dilation, aortic aneurysm, or mitral valve prolapse is reported

data.diagnosis: Remethylation defect causing homocystinuria, such as severe methylenetetrahydrofolate reductase (MTHFR) deficiency
data.description: An inherited defect of homocysteine remethylation that causes hyperhomocysteinemia and may lead to neurologic disease and thrombosis. Unlike CBS deficiency, methionine is usually low or low-normal.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly elevated homocysteine
Normal vitamin B12 level
Normal folic acid level
Potential risk for thrombosis
symptoms_not_in_common: Methionine is markedly elevated rather than low
Ectopia lentis is not a typical feature
Marfanoid skeletal phenotype is not typical
Pectus deformity is not typical
Osteoporosis with vertebral compression changes is less characteristic
No neurologic impairment, seizures, psychiatric symptoms, or developmental delay is reported

data.description: Central nervous system infection by the larval form of Taenia solium. Cysts may occur in the fourth ventricle or subarachnoid spaces and can obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid flow, causing hydrocephalus.
symptoms_in_common: Imaging evidence of a cyst-like lesion in or adjacent to the fourth ventricle/posterior fossa
Ventricular enlargement consistent with obstructive hydrocephalus
Possible small calcified intracranial lesion, which can represent an involuted cysticercus
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as seizures, headache, nausea, vomiting, gait disturbance, or altered consciousness were provided

data.description: A form of neurocysticercosis involving the subarachnoid cisterns or ventricular system, often with larger multilobulated cysts and a greater risk of chronic arachnoiditis and hydrocephalus.
symptoms_in_common: Posterior-fossa/prepontine or cisternal cyst-like abnormalities on imaging
Hydrocephalus or ventricular dilatation
Location near cerebrospinal-fluid pathways where inflammatory obstruction may occur
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported chronic meningitis symptoms, cranial-nerve palsies, headache, nausea, or progressive cognitive decline
A clearly multilobulated grape-like subarachnoid cyst cluster is not definitively demonstrated in the provided images

data.description: A glial tumor arising from ependymal cells, most commonly located in or near the fourth ventricle, where it can obstruct cerebrospinal-fluid flow and cause hydrocephalus.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormality in the fourth-ventricular/posterior-fossa region
Ventricular enlargement compatible with obstructed cerebrospinal-fluid circulation
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears relatively cyst-like/small rather than a typical heterogeneous solid fourth-ventricular mass
No reported headache, vomiting, papilledema, ataxia, cranial-nerve deficits, or other posterior-fossa symptoms
Possible calcified parenchymal lesion is less characteristic of an isolated ependymoma

data.diagnosis: Tuberculoma or tuberculous meningitis with hydrocephalus
data.description: Central nervous system tuberculosis can cause focal granulomas (tuberculomas) or basal meningeal inflammation that obstructs cerebrospinal-fluid circulation and produces hydrocephalus.
symptoms_in_common: Hydrocephalus on imaging
Posterior-fossa/basal cisternal abnormality could occur with inflammatory or granulomatous disease
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, weight loss, night sweats, meningismus, prolonged headache, or altered mental status were provided
The focal cyst-like intraventricular appearance is more suggestive of neurocysticercosis than tuberculoma
No described basal meningeal enhancement or multiple typical enhancing tuberculomas

data.description: Las anomalías de laboratorio durante los primeros 4 días hospitalarios mostraron leucopenia (leucocitos 2100–2200/mm3 tras 7100/mm3 en urgencias) con predominancia linfocitoa, trombocitopenia (126.000 → 80.000 → 75.000 → 84.000/mm3), y anemia leve con caída del hematócrito/hemoglobina (41,3%/14,6 g/dl a 37,9%/13,0 g/dl) y recuentos bajos de reticulocitos. Los marcadores inflamatorios estaban marcadamente elevados (PCR 120,9–178,5 mg/litro, ferritina 7008–8343 ng/ml), con LDH, ALT y AST elevados. El sodio estaba levemente bajo (131–134 mmol/litro), el calcio y la proteína total disminuyeron, y los triglicéridos estaban elevados (282–341 mg/dl). Los estudios de hierro mostraron hierro bajo y baja capacidad de unión al hierro.

Un síndrome hiperinflamatorio potencialmente mortal causado por una activación inmunitaria descontrolada, caracterizado por hemofagocitosis, citopenias, hiperferritinemia, hipertrigliceridemia, lesión hepática e inflamación sistémica.
symptoms_in_common: Leucopenia
Trombocitopenia
Anemia leve con bajo recuento de reticulocitos
Hiperferritinemia marcada (7008–8343 ng/mL)
Hipertrigliceridemia
LDH elevada
AST y ALT elevados
PCR muy elevada
Imágenes de médula ósea compatibles con hemofagagocitosis
Hierro sérico bajo y baja capacidad de unión al hierro, compatibles con la secuestración inflamatoria de hierro
Hipoproteinemia y calcio bajo
symptoms_not_in_common: No se ha reportado fiebre
No se informa explícitamente de esplenomegalia ni hepatomegalia
No se presentan hipofibrinogenemia ni anomalías de coagulación
Solo hay anemia leve en lugar de pancitopenia grave

data.description: Una infección sistémica causada por parásitos Leishmania, endémica en países mediterráneos, incluyendo España. Comúnmente causa fiebre, hepatosplenomegalia, pancitopenia, hepatitis y puede desencadenar HLH secundaria; los amastigotos pueden identificarse en macrófagos de médula ósea.
symptoms_in_common: Residencia en España, donde se produce leishmaniasis visceral mediterránea
Leucopenia con predominancia de linfocitos
Trombocitopenia
Anemia con respuesta reducida de los reticulocitos
Marcadores elevados de ferritina e inflamación
Enzimas hepáticas elevadas
LDH elevada
Hallazgos macrófagos/hemofagocíticos de médula ósea compatibles con HLH asociada a infecciones
Hipertrigliceridemia, que puede ocurrir cuando la leishmaniasis visceral precipita la HLH
symptoms_not_in_common: No se ha reportado fiebre prolongada
No se reportan síntomas de pérdida de peso ni constitucionales
No se informa explícitamente de hepatosplenomegalia
No se reporta hipergammaglobulinemia; en su lugar, la proteína total disminuye
No se proporciona ningún informe directo de Leishmania amastigotes ni pruebas positivas de parásitos

data.description: La HLH puede desencadenarse por malignidades hematológicas, especialmente linfoma de células T o células NK. Produce inflamación severa, citopenias, elevación de ferritina, disfunción hepática y hemofagocitosis de médula.
symptoms_in_common: Leucopenia
Trombocitopenia
Anemia con bajo recuento de reticulocitos
Hiperferritinemia marcada
Hipertrigliceridemia
LDH elevada
Transaminasas elevadas
Hemofagocitosis de la médula
Marcadores inflamatorios altos
symptoms_not_in_common: No se ha notificado linfadenopatía
No se describe ningún hallazgo de imagen específico de lesión masiva ni de linfoma
No se han reportado células linfoides malignas en la médula ósea
No se reportan síntomas B como fiebre, sudores nocturnos ni pérdida de peso

data.description: A chronic invasive bacterial infection, usually caused by Actinomyces species, that can follow dental disease or mucosal trauma and may produce abscesses, draining lesions, necrosis, and destructive osteomyelitis of the mandible or maxilla.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcerated necrotic oral lesion with purulent-appearing material
Extensive destructive changes of the mandible and maxillofacial bones
Findings compatible with chronic osteomyelitis and bony sequestration
Possible extension across contiguous facial structures
symptoms_not_in_common: No typical cervicofacial swelling, cutaneous sinus tracts, or sulfur granules are described
No history of preceding dental extraction, poor dentition, trauma, or immunosuppression is provided
The degree of orbital and midfacial destruction may be more extensive than usual

data.description: A rapidly destructive opportunistic fungal infection caused by Mucorales fungi. It commonly affects the nasal cavity, palate, maxilla, orbit, and adjacent facial bones, producing tissue necrosis and osteomyelitis, particularly in patients with diabetes or immunosuppression.
symptoms_in_common: Necrotic ulcerative lesion in the oral/maxillary region
Marked destruction of maxillary, nasal, orbital, and mandibular bone
Appearance consistent with invasive spread through adjacent facial tissues
Potential palatal or gingival necrosis
symptoms_not_in_common: No diabetes, ketoacidosis, neutropenia, transplant history, corticosteroid use, or other immunosuppression is described
No acute fever, facial pain, nasal black eschar, visual symptoms, or sinus symptoms are reported
Mandibular involvement is less typical than maxillary and sinonasal involvement

data.diagnosis: Advanced oral squamous cell carcinoma with mandibular/maxillary invasion
data.description: Squamous cell carcinoma is the most common malignant tumor of the oral cavity. Advanced lesions may ulcerate, become infected, and invade the mandible, maxilla, floor of mouth, palate, and adjacent facial structures.
symptoms_in_common: Ulcerative oral mucosal lesion
Destructive invasion of jaw bones
Severe irregular osteolytic changes involving the mandible and maxillofacial skeleton
Possible secondary necrosis or infection of the tumor surface
symptoms_not_in_common: No persistent oral pain, bleeding, dysphagia, weight loss, neck mass, or tobacco/alcohol exposure is described
The multifocal and very extensive craniofacial bony destruction could suggest infection or another systemic process rather than a single primary tumor
No biopsy result or discrete soft-tissue mass is provided

data.diagnosis: Medication-related osteonecrosis of the jaw or severe chronic jaw osteomyelitis
data.description: Osteonecrosis of the jaw can occur after antiresorptive or antiangiogenic medication exposure, especially following dental procedures. It presents with exposed necrotic bone, chronic ulceration, secondary infection, sequestra, and progressive mandibular or maxillary destruction.
symptoms_in_common: Oral ulceration overlying abnormal jaw bone
Necrotic-appearing tissue and possible exposed bone or sequestrum
Severe mandibular and maxillary osteolysis compatible with chronic osteomyelitis/osteonecrosis
Potential secondary oral infection
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of bisphosphonate, denosumab, antiangiogenic therapy, radiotherapy, or recent dental extraction is provided
Orbital, nasal, and broad midfacial destruction is not typical of isolated medication-related jaw osteonecrosis
No chronic jaw pain, loose teeth, or exposed bone duration is reported

data.description: An inflammatory granulomatous disease in which noncaseating granulomas infiltrate the myocardium, potentially causing conduction abnormalities, arrhythmias, heart failure, and sudden cardiac death.
symptoms_in_common: Electrocardiographic conduction abnormality/possible bundle-branch block pattern
Chest radiograph with cardiac enlargement and bilateral interstitial-pulmonary changes
Myocardial biopsy showing granulomatous inflammation with multinucleated giant cells
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as palpitations, syncope, chest pain, dyspnea, fever, or extracardiac sarcoidosis manifestations were provided

data.description: A rare, often rapidly progressive autoimmune myocarditis characterized by myocardial inflammation, multinucleated giant cells, ventricular arrhythmias, heart block, and heart failure.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal ECG with conduction-system involvement
Possible cardiomegaly on chest radiograph
Myocardial inflammatory infiltrate containing multinucleated giant cells
symptoms_not_in_common: Organized granulomatous inflammation is more characteristic of sarcoidosis than classic giant cell myocarditis
No reported rapidly progressive heart failure
No reported sustained ventricular tachycardia, syncope, or cardiogenic shock

data.description: Myocardial involvement by Mycobacterium tuberculosis is rare and may produce granulomas, conduction defects, arrhythmias, ventricular dysfunction, or pericardial disease.
symptoms_in_common: Granulomatous myocardial inflammation with giant cells on biopsy
Possible pulmonary/interstitial radiographic abnormalities
Cardiac conduction abnormality on ECG
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever, night sweats, weight loss, chronic cough, or tuberculosis exposure was provided
No caseating necrosis or acid-fast bacilli were described on the biopsy
No pleural effusion or typical pulmonary tuberculosis pattern was reported

data.diagnosis: Cardiac involvement from fungal granulomatous infection
data.description: Disseminated fungal infections can rarely cause granulomatous myocarditis, sometimes with giant cells, conduction defects, and myocardial dysfunction.
symptoms_in_common: Granulomatous inflammatory infiltrates in myocardial tissue
Multinucleated giant cells
Possible pulmonary radiographic abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: No immunosuppression, fever, systemic infection, or fungal exposure history was provided
No fungal organisms were described on histology
No reported respiratory or constitutional symptoms

data.diagnosis: Andersen-Tawil syndrome type 1 (KCNJ2-related disorder, long QT syndrome type 7)
data.description: A rare autosomal-dominant channelopathy caused by pathogenic KCNJ2 variants. It classically causes ventricular arrhythmias, periodic paralysis, and characteristic skeletal/facial features.
symptoms_in_common: Heterozygous KCNJ2 variant c.1216G>A, p.(Gly406Arg)
Bilateral hand skeletal abnormalities consistent with clinodactyly/brachydactyly
Ventricular ectopy and complex ventricular arrhythmia pattern on ECG/Holter recordings
Prominent U waves and prolonged QU interval appearance on ECG

data.description: An inherited arrhythmia syndrome characterized by exercise- or emotion-induced bidirectional or polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, usually in patients with structurally normal hearts.
symptoms_in_common: Complex ventricular ectopy
Possible bidirectional/polymorphic ventricular tachycardia pattern
symptoms_not_in_common: Bilateral hand skeletal abnormalities
KCNJ2 p.(Gly406Arg) variant, which is more characteristic of Andersen-Tawil syndrome
Prominent U-wave/QU-interval abnormality

data.diagnosis: Long QT syndrome due to another ion-channel disorder
data.description: A group of inherited cardiac channelopathies causing delayed ventricular repolarization and increased risk of ventricular arrhythmias, syncope, and sudden cardiac death.
symptoms_in_common: Abnormal ventricular repolarization pattern on ECG
Ventricular arrhythmias/ectopy
symptoms_not_in_common: Characteristic bilateral hand skeletal abnormalities
KCNJ2 p.(Gly406Arg) variant specifically supports long QT syndrome type 7/Andersen-Tawil syndrome rather than most other long QT syndromes
The combination of dysmorphic skeletal findings and ventricular ectopy is not typical of most other long QT subtypes

data.description: Marked leukocytosis on outpatient testing the day before admission and again on admission (WBC 146,700 and 145,400/mm³) with extreme eosinophilia (70–83%; absolute eosinophils 120,690/mm³), mild thrombocytosis (440,000–483,000/mm³), and elevated prothrombin time (16.3 sec). Other notable labs on admission included hyponatremia (133 mmol/L), low glucose (44 mg/dL), low albumin (3.2 g/dL), low phosphorus (2.4 mg/dL), low calcium (8.4 mg/dL), elevated alkaline phosphatase (232 U/L), AST (163 U/L), and LDH (322 U/L). Hematocrit was 41.6% outpatient and 40.0% on admission.

data.diagnosis: Chronic eosinophilic leukemia, particularly FIP1L1-PDGFRA-rearranged myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm with eosinophilia
data.description: A clonal myeloid neoplasm characterized by persistent marked eosinophilia, often with hypercellular bone marrow and eosinophilic infiltration of organs. PDGFRA-rearranged disease can present with very high eosinophil counts and is typically highly responsive to imatinib.
symptoms_in_common: Extreme persistent leukocytosis (WBC approximately 145,000/mm³)
Extreme absolute eosinophilia (approximately 120,690/mm³)
Eosinophils comprising 70–83% of circulating leukocytes
Mild thrombocytosis
Bone marrow appearance with marked eosinophilic hyperplasia
Possible gastrointestinal tissue eosinophilic infiltration on biopsy
Elevated LDH
Elevated alkaline phosphatase and AST, potentially reflecting organ involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Hypoglycemia
Mild hyponatremia
Low phosphorus
Low calcium
Elevated prothrombin time

data.description: A syndrome of sustained marked eosinophilia with eosinophil-mediated tissue or organ injury after exclusion of secondary causes, including parasites, drugs, allergic disease, autoimmune disease, and clonal hematologic neoplasms.
symptoms_in_common: Severe persistent eosinophilia
Very high total leukocyte count
Apparent eosinophilic infiltration of bone marrow
Possible colonic or gastrointestinal eosinophilic inflammation
Abnormal liver enzymes that may indicate organ involvement
Elevated LDH

Hypoglycemia
Prolonged prothrombin time
Hyponatremia

data.diagnosis: Reactive eosinophilia due to helminthic parasitic infection, such as strongyloidiasis or toxocariasis
data.description: Tissue-invasive helminth infections can produce eosinophilia, gastrointestinal inflammation, hepatic enzyme abnormalities, and occasionally eosinophilic infiltrates in involved tissues. Exposure history, stool testing, serology, and travel history are needed for confirmation.
symptoms_in_common: Marked eosinophilia
Leukocytosis
Possible gastrointestinal eosinophilic inflammation in the biopsy
Elevated AST and alkaline phosphatase, which can occur with hepatic involvement
Low albumin, which can occur with gastrointestinal disease or systemic inflammation
symptoms_not_in_common: Absolute eosinophil count of approximately 120,690/mm³ is far more extreme than is typical for most helminth infections
Persistent WBC count around 145,000/mm³ is unusual for uncomplicated parasitic infection
Mild thrombocytosis is not a defining feature
Bone marrow findings dominated by massive eosinophilic proliferation may favor a clonal hematologic disorder
Hypoglycemia
Prolonged prothrombin time

data.diagnosis: Systemic mastocytosis with associated hematologic neoplasm or another myeloid neoplasm with eosinophilia
data.description: Systemic mast cell disease may coexist with a myeloid neoplasm and can cause eosinophilia, marrow abnormalities, hepatobiliary dysfunction, and constitutional or gastrointestinal manifestations. This diagnosis would require marrow mast-cell aggregates and appropriate immunophenotypic and molecular studies.

Leukocytosis
Possible marrow hypercellularity
Mild thrombocytosis
Elevated alkaline phosphatase and AST, which may occur with hepatic involvement
Low albumin
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported flushing, urticaria pigmentosa, anaphylaxis, pruritus, or recurrent hypotensive episodes

Hypoglycemia
Hyponatremia
Extreme eosinophilia alone is more directly suggestive of a primary eosinophilic neoplasm

data.diagnosis: Hodgkin lymphoma or T-cell lymphoma with paraneoplastic eosinophilia
data.description: Some lymphomas, particularly Hodgkin lymphoma and certain T-cell lymphomas, can produce cytokines such as IL-5 that drive eosinophilia. These disorders generally cause lymphadenopathy, constitutional symptoms, and less often severe leukemoid eosinophilia.
symptoms_in_common: Leukocytosis
Eosinophilia
Elevated LDH
Low albumin
Abnormal liver enzymes may occur with systemic or hepatic involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: Absolute eosinophil count greater than 120,000/mm³ is unusually extreme for lymphoma-associated eosinophilia
No reported lymphadenopathy
No reported fever, night sweats, weight loss, or pruritus
Mild thrombocytosis is nonspecific
Bone marrow predominance of eosinophils may favor a primary myeloid eosinophilic disorder
Hypoglycemia
Low phosphorus and low calcium

data.description: An aggressive diffuse astrocytic glioma, usually with necrosis, vascular proliferation, hemorrhage, marked edema, and ring enhancement. The immunoprofile shown is compatible with a glial tumor: GFAP and Olig2 positivity, absent IDH1 R132H staining, retained ATRX expression, p53 positivity, and increased proliferative activity.

Irregular thick ring enhancement on MRI
Central necrotic or hemorrhagic component
Marked surrounding vasogenic edema
Mass effect
Hyperdense intratumoral hemorrhage on noncontrast CT
GFAP-positive and Olig2-positive tumor cells
IDH1 immunostaining negative
Elevated MIB-1/Ki-67 proliferative labeling
symptoms_not_in_common: No patient-reported clinical symptoms were provided
No multifocal brain lesions are shown
No vascular malformation or aneurysm is apparent on the supplied vascular imaging

data.diagnosis: Diffuse astrocytoma, IDH-wildtype with high-grade features
data.description: A diffusely infiltrating astrocytic tumor lacking the common IDH1 R132H mutation by immunohistochemistry. In an adult, an IDH-wildtype diffuse astrocytic tumor with necrosis, hemorrhage, ring enhancement, and high proliferation is generally biologically similar to glioblastoma.
symptoms_in_common: Intra-axial cerebral mass in the frontal lobe
Astrocytic differentiation suggested by GFAP positivity
Olig2-positive glial neoplastic cells
Negative IDH1 R132H immunostaining
ATRX expression appears retained
p53 immunoreactivity
Perilesional edema and mass effect
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent ring enhancement and necrosis are more typical of glioblastoma than lower-grade diffuse astrocytoma
Intratumoral hemorrhage is less typical of a lower-grade astrocytoma
High proliferative activity is less typical of a lower-grade tumor
No patient-reported clinical symptoms were provided

data.description: A metastatic systemic cancer deposit in the brain can present as a well-circumscribed ring-enhancing lesion with extensive vasogenic edema and intralesional hemorrhage. Certain metastases, such as melanoma, renal cell carcinoma, thyroid carcinoma, and choriocarcinoma, may bleed.
symptoms_in_common: Solitary ring-enhancing cerebral lesion
Extensive surrounding vasogenic edema
Mass effect
Intralesional hemorrhage on CT
Relatively circumscribed mass-like appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: GFAP positivity supports glial differentiation rather than a typical metastatic carcinoma
Olig2 positivity supports primary glial neoplasia rather than most metastases
No known extracranial primary malignancy was provided
No patient-reported systemic cancer symptoms were provided

data.description: A focal intracerebral infection containing purulent material, often producing a ring-enhancing lesion with surrounding edema and mass effect. Diffusion restriction and clinical evidence of infection are usually important diagnostic clues.
symptoms_in_common: Ring-enhancing intracerebral lesion
Central nonenhancing component
Marked surrounding edema
Mass effect
symptoms_not_in_common: Intratumoral hemorrhage is not a typical dominant feature of a pyogenic abscess

data.description: A fungal infection caused by Cryptococcus species that can disseminate from the lungs to bone, producing vertebral osteomyelitis and paravertebral soft-tissue masses, particularly in immunocompromised patients but occasionally in immunocompetent individuals.

Pulmonary/mediastinal abnormalities that may represent prior or disseminated fungal infection

Vertebral osteomyelitis-like destructive lesion
Associated paravertebral inflammatory soft-tissue mass
Fungal organisms visible on tissue staining

Paravertebral soft-tissue extension

Round fungal structures in tissue that could represent fungal spherules

Spain is a region where tuberculosis occurs

data.diagnosis: Disseminated Lomentospora prolificans infection (formerly Scedosporium prolificans)

Inflammatory and necrotic-appearing tissue
Fungal hyphae visible in tissue sections
Concurrent pulmonary and extrapulmonary disease compatible with hematogenous dissemination

data.diagnosis: Spastic paraplegia type 11 (SPG11), also called hereditary spastic paraplegia with thin corpus callosum
data.description: An autosomal-recessive complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia caused by biallelic pathogenic variants in SPG11. It commonly produces progressive lower-limb spasticity and weakness, cognitive impairment, dysarthria, peripheral neuropathy, and thinning of the corpus callosum on brain MRI.
symptoms_in_common: Biallelic SPG11 frameshift variants (p.M245fs and p.F2343fs)
Young-adult onset
Lower-limb weakness
Hyperreflexia
Babinski signs
Clonus
Dysarthria
Intellectual disability/mental retardation
MRI appearance consistent with thinning of the corpus callosum and periventricular white-matter changes

data.description: A group of inherited neurodegenerative disorders characterized by progressive corticospinal-tract dysfunction causing spastic paraparesis. Complicated forms additionally involve cognitive impairment, dysarthria, neuropathy, ataxia, seizures, or characteristic brain-imaging abnormalities.
symptoms_in_common: Lower-limb weakness
Hyperreflexia
Babinski signs
Clonus
Dysarthria
Intellectual disability
Corpus callosum abnormality on MRI
Recessive genetic pattern suggested by two SPG11 variants
symptoms_not_in_common: No atypical symptoms are specifically documented; the SPG11 genotype makes a more specific SPG11 diagnosis more likely than an unspecified hereditary spastic paraplegia

data.diagnosis: Hereditary spastic paraplegia with thin corpus callosum (HSP-TCC phenotype)
data.description: A clinical-radiologic syndrome of complicated hereditary spastic paraplegia featuring spastic paraparesis with a thin corpus callosum, cognitive impairment, and white-matter abnormalities. SPG11 is the most frequent genetic cause.
symptoms_in_common: Spastic pyramidal signs including hyperreflexia, Babinski signs, and clonus
Lower-limb weakness
Cognitive impairment
Dysarthria
Thin corpus callosum on sagittal MRI
Periventricular white-matter signal abnormalities
symptoms_not_in_common: Upper-limb hyperreflexia may occur in advanced disease but is less central than lower-limb-predominant spasticity

data.description: A rare, highly vascular neuroendocrine tumor arising from paraganglionic tissue, often located near the atrioventricular grooves or great vessels. These tumors may show intense FDG uptake and avid contrast enhancement on cardiac imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Intensely FDG-avid cardiac mass on PET imaging
Well-defined mass near the atrioventricular groove
Marked enhancement/hypervascular appearance on cardiac MRI
Apparent relationship to coronary vessels
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as episodic hypertension, palpitations, diaphoresis, headache, or catecholamine excess are provided

data.description: A malignant lymphoid tumor involving the heart, most often affecting the right atrium, right ventricle, pericardium, or atrioventricular groove. It is typically strongly FDG-avid.
symptoms_in_common: Markedly FDG-avid cardiac lesion
Mass involving the right-sided cardiac/atrioventricular-groove region
Soft-tissue cardiac mass on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: The lesion appears relatively circumscribed and hypervascular, which is more characteristic of paraganglioma than lymphoma
No systemic symptoms such as fever, weight loss, night sweats, or immunosuppression are provided
No pericardial effusion or diffuse infiltrative cardiac involvement is described

data.description: An aggressive malignant vascular tumor of the heart that most commonly arises in the right atrium and can demonstrate FDG uptake and contrast enhancement due to its vascular nature.
symptoms_in_common: Cardiac mass in a right-sided cardiac region
FDG uptake on PET imaging
Enhancing lesion on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Angiosarcomas more commonly arise from the right atrial free wall rather than the atrioventricular groove
Angiosarcomas are often infiltrative, heterogeneous, and associated with pericardial effusion or metastases, none of which are provided
No symptoms such as dyspnea, chest pain, right-sided heart failure, or pericardial tamponade are reported

data.description: A focal central nervous system infection caused by Nocardia species, aerobic Gram-positive branching bacteria that can produce multiloculated abscesses and may disseminate from the lungs or skin.
symptoms_in_common: Ring-enhancing intracerebral lesion with surrounding edema
Restricted diffusion within the lesion, compatible with purulent material
Necrotic/suppurative pathology with abundant neutrophilic inflammation
Microscopic appearance compatible with filamentous or branching bacterial organisms
Mass-spectrometry pattern consistent with bacterial identification

data.description: A localized collection of pus in the brain caused by bacteria, commonly producing a ring-enhancing lesion with central restricted diffusion and surrounding vasogenic edema.
symptoms_in_common: Ring-enhancing cerebral lesion
Central diffusion restriction
Extensive surrounding edema
Suppurative inflammation with numerous neutrophils
Possible bacterial organisms on tissue staining
symptoms_not_in_common: Branching filamentous bacterial morphology would be more suggestive of Nocardia or Actinomyces than of common pyogenic bacteria

data.description: An uncommon chronic bacterial infection caused by Actinomyces species, anaerobic or microaerophilic Gram-positive branching rods that can occasionally form intracranial abscesses.
symptoms_in_common: Brain abscess with ring enhancement and edema
Purulent inflammatory tissue with neutrophils
Possible branching Gram-positive bacillary organisms
symptoms_not_in_common: Actinomyces infections more often have an associated dental, sinus, otologic, or cervicofacial source, which is not reported
The imaging appearance is not specifically characteristic of Actinomyces

data.description: An opportunistic infection caused by Toxoplasma gondii that commonly produces multiple ring-enhancing brain lesions, particularly in people with advanced HIV infection or other severe immunosuppression.
symptoms_in_common: Ring-enhancing intracranial lesion
Surrounding cerebral edema
Necrotic lesion appearance
symptoms_not_in_common: Restricted diffusion and marked neutrophilic suppuration are more typical of a bacterial abscess
Histologic evidence of bacterial-type organisms is not typical
No immunosuppression, HIV infection, or multiple basal-ganglia lesions are reported

data.diagnosis: Glioblastoma or other necrotic high-grade glioma
data.description: A malignant primary brain tumor that can show irregular ring enhancement, central necrosis, edema, and mass effect, sometimes mimicking an abscess on imaging.
symptoms_in_common: Enhancing intracerebral mass
Central necrotic-appearing component
Extensive surrounding edema
symptoms_not_in_common: Central restricted diffusion favors pus-containing abscess over necrotic tumor

Bacterial organisms or bacterial mass-spectrometry findings are not typical of a primary brain tumor

Lower-lung predominance on imaging
Multifocal rather than a single sharply lobar pattern of disease

data.diagnosis: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis related to environmental water or mold exposure
data.description: An immune-mediated inflammatory lung disease caused by inhaled environmental antigens, including molds or aerosolized organisms from damp buildings or water exposures.

Bilateral pulmonary opacities

data.description: Electrophysiologic and ultrastructural measurements showed reduced MEPP amplitude (0.43 ± 0.05 mV vs 1.24 ± 0.15 in controls), reduced MEPC amplitude (1.29 ± 0.05 nA vs 4.55 ± 0.28), reduced EPP quantal content at 1 Hz (6.79 ± 1.48 vs 12.71 ± 1.60), and lower E/I ratio (4.99 ± 0.34 vs 11.71 ± 2.36). Secondary clefts per junction were 1.45 ± 0.1, nerve terminal area was 7.28 ± 1.06 µm², and synaptic vesicle density was 13.48 ± 4.62/µm.

Reduced EPP quantal content

Reduced nerve-terminal area
Reduced synaptic-vesicle density

Reduced MEPC amplitude
Reduced quantal content of EPPs
Low EPP/MEPP ratio

Reduced synaptic-vesicle density

data.diagnosis: Congenital myasthenic syndrome due to LRP4 mutation

symptoms_in_common: Reduced miniature endplate potential amplitude
Reduced miniature endplate current amplitude
Reduced evoked quantal release
Decreased EPP/MEPP ratio
Reduced postsynaptic junctional folding
Abnormal presynaptic terminal morphology
Decreased synaptic-vesicle density

data.diagnosis: Acetylcholine receptor deficiency congenital myasthenic syndrome
data.description: A postsynaptic congenital myasthenic syndrome, often caused by mutations in acetylcholine-receptor subunit genes such as CHRNE, resulting in reduced functional acetylcholine receptors at the endplate.

Reduced MEPC amplitude
Low EPP/MEPP ratio consistent with impaired postsynaptic responsiveness

data.description: A congenital myasthenic syndrome caused by rapsyn deficiency, impairing clustering and stabilization of acetylcholine receptors at the postsynaptic membrane.
symptoms_in_common: Reduced MEPP amplitude
Reduced MEPC amplitude
Reduced safety factor of neuromuscular transmission reflected by a low EPP/MEPP ratio
Reduced complexity of postsynaptic folds may be present
Abnormal neuromuscular-junction ultrastructure
symptoms_not_in_common: Substantially reduced EPP quantal content is less typical as the principal abnormality
Reduced nerve-terminal area is not usually a primary feature
Reduced synaptic-vesicle density is not usually a primary feature

symptoms_not_in_common: No recurrent kidney stones reported

No hematuria reported
No gastrointestinal malabsorption symptoms reported
No family history or prior stone history reported

A zoonotic infection caused by Bartonella henselae, usually transmitted through a cat scratch, bite, or flea exposure. Lymph node histology with necrotizing granulomatous/suppurative inflammatory areas
Demonstration of bacillary organisms by special stain/immunohistochemistry
Mild leukocytosis on presentation
Marked neutrophilia
Mild anemia
symptoms_not_in_common: No cat exposure, scratch, bite, or inoculation-site skin lesion is reported

No constitutional symptoms such as fatigue, weight loss, or night sweats are reported

Necrotizing/suppurative granulomatous lymph node inflammation
Leukocytosis with neutrophilia

data.diagnosis: Arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy (ARVC), also called arrhythmogenic right ventricular dysplasia

symptoms_in_common: Mites visible within the stratum corneum on histology
Inflammatory skin lesions
Erosions and ulceration
Crusted and excoriated scalp lesions
Multiple erythematous plaques and erosions on the trunk
symptoms_not_in_common: Prominent scalp involvement is less typical in immunocompetent adults but may occur in infants, elderly patients, or severe infestation

data.description: A severe form of scabies with a very high mite burden, often producing extensive crusting, hyperkeratosis, erosions, ulceration, and widespread inflammatory lesions. It is more likely in people with impaired immunity, neurologic disease, disability, or inability to scratch.
symptoms_in_common: Mites identified in the superficial epidermis
Extensive inflamed, crusted, and ulcerated skin lesions
Scalp involvement
Widespread trunk lesions
Multiple erosive plaques
symptoms_not_in_common: The images do not clearly show the thick, diffuse hyperkeratotic crusts classically associated with severe crusted scabies
No immune suppression, neurologic disease, or reduced sensation is reported

data.diagnosis: Scabies with secondary bacterial infection (impetiginized scabies)
data.description: Scabies lesions may become secondarily infected, commonly with Staphylococcus aureus or Streptococcus pyogenes, producing painful erosions, ulceration, crusting, purulent drainage, or impetigo-like lesions.
symptoms_in_common: Scabies mite present on biopsy
Ulcerated and crusted lesions
Marked inflammatory infiltrate in the dermis
Erosive lesions on the scalp and trunk
Areas that appear excoriated or possibly infected
symptoms_not_in_common: No fever or systemic illness is described
No purulent drainage, honey-colored crusting, bacterial culture result, or cellulitis is reported

data.description: An immune-complex-mediated kidney disease characterized by mesangial proliferation, lobulated glomeruli, and thickening or duplication of glomerular capillary walls.
symptoms_in_common: Renal-biopsy image showing a hypercellular, lobulated glomerulus with mesangial expansion and apparent capillary-wall remodeling
symptoms_not_in_common: No clinical symptoms such as edema, hematuria, hypertension, or proteinuria were provided

data.description: A common immune-mediated glomerulonephritis caused by mesangial deposition of IgA, often producing mesangial hypercellularity and recurrent blood in the urine.
symptoms_in_common: Glomerular mesangial proliferation/hypercellularity suggested by the biopsy image
May occur in patients in Spain and other European countries
symptoms_not_in_common: No episodes of visible or microscopic hematuria were provided
No proteinuria, edema, or hypertension were provided
IgA deposits cannot be confirmed from this image alone without immunofluorescence

data.description: Kidney inflammation caused by systemic lupus erythematosus, often producing proliferative glomerular lesions with marked mesangial and endocapillary hypercellularity.
symptoms_in_common: Proliferative glomerular lesion suggested by the biopsy image
Mesangial expansion and increased glomerular cellularity may be seen in lupus nephritis
symptoms_not_in_common: No history of systemic lupus erythematosus was provided
No rash, photosensitivity, arthritis, fever, or other systemic autoimmune symptoms were provided
No hematuria, proteinuria, edema, or hypertension were provided

data.description: A severe form of glomerular inflammation that can cause rapid loss of kidney function and may show extracapillary cellular proliferation (crescents) on biopsy.
symptoms_in_common: Biopsy image suggests substantial glomerular inflammation and hypercellularity
symptoms_not_in_common: No rapidly worsening kidney function was provided
No oliguria, hematuria, hypertension, or edema were provided
A definite crescent cannot be confirmed from the supplied image alone

data.description: A rare benign inflammatory disorder characterized by dense eosinophil infiltration of the bile ducts, producing biliary wall thickening, strictures, and obstruction that may mimic cholangiocarcinoma.
symptoms_in_common: Intrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation and/or focal biliary stricture on CT and MRCP
Inflammatory lesion near the hepatic hilum
Dense eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate surrounding bile ducts on histology
Immunohistochemical staining highlighting eosinophilic inflammatory cells

data.description: A malignant tumor arising from bile duct epithelium, commonly presenting as a hilar or intrahepatic biliary stricture with upstream bile duct dilatation.
symptoms_in_common: Hilar/periductal abnormality on CT
Biliary narrowing with upstream intrahepatic duct dilatation on MRCP
Appearance that can resemble an obstructing bile duct tumor
symptoms_not_in_common: Histology shows prominent eosinophilic inflammation rather than malignant atypical gland-forming cells
No definite invasive malignant epithelial tumor is evident in the provided histology

data.description: An immune-mediated fibroinflammatory disease causing bile duct wall thickening and strictures, often associated with autoimmune pancreatitis and increased IgG4-positive plasma cells.
symptoms_in_common: Biliary stricturing and intrahepatic biliary dilatation
Inflammatory tissue around bile ducts
Can radiologically mimic cholangiocarcinoma or primary sclerosing cholangitis
symptoms_not_in_common: The provided histology is dominated by eosinophils rather than the typical dense lymphoplasmacytic infiltrate
No stated storiform fibrosis or obliterative phlebitis
No stated increase in IgG4-positive plasma cells or autoimmune pancreatitis

data.description: Infection with the liver fluke Fasciola hepatica, which is encountered in parts of Spain and can cause eosinophilic hepatic inflammation, biliary obstruction, and cholangitis.
symptoms_in_common: Residence in Spain, where Fasciola hepatica infection can occur
Eosinophil-rich inflammatory infiltrate
Biliary tract abnormality with ductal dilatation or obstruction
symptoms_not_in_common: No parasite, ova, or fluke fragments are shown in the supplied histology
No stated peripheral eosinophilia, fever, right-upper-quadrant pain, or exposure to contaminated aquatic plants
